At the same time, KD is bounded by data availability, teacher quality, capacity mismatch, and potential transfer of undesirable teacher behaviors, so it is best used as part of an integrated compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Strong
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesized Review
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and richer internal information. A broad toolbox of distillation targets and protocols has emerged—soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free sample synthesis, self- and online-distillation, and multi-teacher schemes—and these are routinely combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD has been applied across vision, language, graphs, speech, generative models, and federated settings, yielding large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance when design choices are task- and architecture-aware. Remaining challenges include teacher–student mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, data scarcity or privacy constraints, and instability in optimization; practical remedies emphasize task-aware signal selection, learned teacher adaptation, layer mapping strategies, and data-synthesis or privacy-preserving protocols. This review synthesizes empirical patterns, common mechanisms, practical recommendations, and open problems for KD-driven compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Stephens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applied strategy for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teachers into compact students. Across modalities, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while often preserving much of teacher performance. Success depends on the choice of distilled signals, teacher and student design, data availability, and integration with complementary compression techniques; awareness of practical failure modes such as capacity mismatch, optimization difficulty, distribution shift, and transferred biases is essential. This synthesis summarizes what is known about KD methods, practical integrations with other compression approaches, representative applications, common limitations, and recommended design principles for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Simon

While KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and supports domain adaptation, privacy-aware training, and robustness improvements, its practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and alignment, and careful objective and architecture design; therefore KD should be treated as a central element of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable family of techniques that transfers information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while often retaining much of the teacher’s performance. The literature shows a diverse toolkit of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure, channel statistics, and contrastive signals), protocols (offline, online, self-, multi-teacher, and data-free variants), and task-aware adaptations (layer mapping, projector modules, synthetic-data generation, and curriculum/annealing). Empirical work across vision, language, graphs, multimodal tasks, and continual or federated settings demonstrates substantial efficiency gains but also highlights persistent challenges: teacher–student capacity and architecture mismatch, limited or unavailable training data, propagation of teacher biases or errors, distribution shift, and difficulties transferring rare or low-frequency behaviors. Practical success typically requires matching the distillation signal to task and student capacity and integrating KD with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Context‑Aware, and Insufficient Alone for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and empirically validated family of techniques that reliably improves the efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs of deep models across modalities. KD enables deployment by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller students, and it supports many training protocols and transfer targets. However, KD is not a standalone solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the availability or synthesis of suitable data, and careful mitigation of failure modes (distribution shift, low-frequency degradation, and bias propagation). Therefore, for robust real-world deployment KD should be treated as a configurable, task‑aware core of an integrated compression pipeline that combines complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design), teacher–student co‑design, and data strategies tailored to the application.

papers_seen.author: Moon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers. When treated as a configurable component of a compression pipeline and adapted to teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of a teacher's performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. However, KD is not a turnkey cure: it must be combined with projector or layer-mapping techniques, ensemble and adversarial strategies where appropriate, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) while explicitly mitigating failure modes such as bias transfer, low-frequency degradation, and data scarcity. Continued theoretical and empirical work is needed to standardize best practices, automate signal selection, and robustly distill structured or generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Walker

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for producing compact, deployable neural models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational or contrastive signals) and across diverse protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, and data-free/privacy-aware schemes). When combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, KD routinely enables large reductions in latency, memory, and compute while preserving much of teacher performance. Its empirical success is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and synthesis strategies, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, distribution shift, and degradation on low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become central strategies for deploying large deep models under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. A diverse set of methods—ranging from soft-label distillation, intermediate feature and attention matching, layer mapping, adversarial and data-free techniques, to task-adaptive architecture search and meta-learning of teachers—have been proposed to transfer performance from bulky teachers to compact students. These approaches are applied across domains including vision, language, multi-modal systems, recommender systems, and domain-specific NLP, and they trade off fidelity to the teacher, generalization, and computational efficiency. Empirical results show that properly designed distillation pipelines can recover a large fraction of teacher performance while yielding substantial speedups and memory reductions, and in some settings can even improve fairness, robustness, or downstream generalization. Remaining challenges include aligning heterogeneous inputs and representations across teacher and student, coping with absent or private training data, and automatically selecting what and how to transfer for specific tasks and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Reese
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Core, Configurable, and Context‑Aware for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with careful teacher–student design, data strategies, and complementary primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design—KD routinely yields efficient models that retain much of teacher performance. Its benefits span modalities and deployment settings, but real-world success requires explicit attention to capacity mismatch, data limitations, bias propagation, and distribution shift. Consequently, KD should be the default first-line compression tool but must be applied with task-aware protocols and safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Levy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Dependent Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic set of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or specialized models by transferring behavior and representations from larger teachers. When integrated with complementary compression methods and task-aware engineering, KD routinely enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and communication while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, available data, and objective design, and it raises open challenges in robustness, privacy, and automatic student design.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become primary approaches for deploying high-performing deep models in resource-constrained settings. The literature spans methods that transfer soft-labels, internal feature representations, and ensemble knowledge; extensions address teacher imperfections, data scarcity or privacy, task-specific adaptations for NLP and vision, and hardware-aware compression. Empirical work demonstrates that careful design choices—such as which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student layers, whether to incorporate self-distillation or multi-teacher training, and how to combine pruning or low-precision numerics—substantially affect final accuracy and efficiency. The field also benefits from theoretical analyses that clarify when and why distillation helps. Remaining challenges include distilling robust semantics for low-frequency phenomena, distillation without access to original data, and co-design for hardware deployment.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Tool for Reliable Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely applicable approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. When treated as a configurable, task-aware component of a broader compression pipeline, KD can deliver substantial gains in latency, memory, and often accuracy while enabling deployment in resource- and privacy-constrained settings. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, signal selection, and complementary compression methods. Responsible application requires explicit mitigation of failure modes such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and bias transfer, and integration with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, or data‑free methods when appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a broad family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, more efficient student models to meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals) and within diverse protocols (offline teacher→student, online/self-distillation, multi‑teacher, and data‑free/zero‑shot approaches). Empirical evidence shows KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance and can sometimes improve student generalization when objectives, data, and teacher–student design are well matched; however, success is context dependent and sensitive to teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and distribution shift, and risks of transferring teacher errors or bias. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that combines carefully chosen distillation signals, layer-mapping and curriculum strategies, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture search) while adopting targeted safeguards for low‑frequency behaviors, privacy, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are now core tools for producing smaller, faster models while retaining much of the performance and functionality of larger teachers. The literature has expanded far beyond simple logits matching to include feature- and representation-level transfer, many-to-many layer mapping, contrastive and adversarial objectives, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, multi-teacher and teacher-engineering strategies, and tight integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work demonstrates broad applicability across modalities (vision, NLP, speech, graphs, and generative models) and deployment contexts (edge devices, federated systems, and data-constrained settings). The main practical challenges are (1) choosing what and how to distill for a given task and student architecture, (2) coping with limited or unavailable original training data, (3) avoiding transfer of teacher weaknesses (e.g., biases or low-frequency degradation), and (4) co-designing distillation with other compression primitives and hardware constraints. Progress comes from combining representational objectives, layer-mapping strategies, task-aware teacher selection, and safeguards (privacy or fairness) appropriate to deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Brooks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically effective approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers. When treated as a configurable component of a compression pipeline and adapted to teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of a teacher's performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: its effectiveness depends on signal selection, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and integration with complementary compression methods; responsible use requires mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, low‑frequency degradation, and privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Ruiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring behavior from large or ensemble teacher models to smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants — including soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free synthesis — are used alone or with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to reduce parameters, latency, and memory while attempting to retain teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to task and student capacity, handling limited or private data, and mitigating transferred biases or rare-case failures. Important open problems include teacher–student capacity gaps, domain shift and data scarcity, privacy guarantees for data-free and federated settings, and automated teacher–student co-design for hardware-aware deployment.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical, and theoretically grounded approach to compressing and adapting deep models. Across modalities and tasks, KD enables compact students to inherit predictive performance, inductive biases, and application-specific properties (privacy, fairness, task-adaptivity) from larger or specialized teachers. Best practice combines logit-level, feature-level, and architecture-aware strategies, often augmented by multi-teacher, curriculum, or meta-learning schemes; privacy-preserving and data-free variants make KD suitable for sensitive or decentralized settings. We argue that KD should be a first-class tool in compression toolkits and outline concrete practices that are supported by empirical and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: The Promise and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central method for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, KD variants enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, promote interpretable surrogates, and support ensemble compression. However, KD also transfers teacher biases, faces optimization and data-distribution challenges, and requires careful choices of objectives, data augmentation, and teacher-student protocols to be effective in practice.

papers_seen.author: Salazar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a broad, practically driven family of methods that transfer predictive behavior, internal representations, or structured information from large teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Techniques span logits/soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level alignment, channel- and layer-wise objectives, self- and multi-teacher designs, data-free and few-shot protocols, and adversarial or generator-based data synthesis. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful data and training practices, distillation often preserves much of the teacher's performance and can add functional guarantees (robustness, low-precision accuracy, privacy-aware releases). Key limitations include dependence on teacher quality, student capacity and architectural alignment, distributional mismatch or limited data, and the risk of propagating teacher errors or biases, motivating continued work on principled objectives, data strategies, and deployment-aware pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical framework for producing smaller, faster, and deployable models from larger teachers across vision, language, speech, and multimodal settings. Research has expanded KD beyond logits-only supervision into a rich set of objectives (feature and representation matching, relational and contrastive signals, adversarial/data-free schemes, and self-distillation), and into diverse data regimes from full-data to data-free, few-shot, federated, and privacy-constrained workflows. KD is frequently combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search, low-precision numerics) and with teacher-aware or student-aware design choices; its empirical success depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and data strategies. Remaining challenges include handling architecture and distributional mismatch, avoiding propagation of teacher errors and biases (especially on low-frequency phenomena), providing privacy and robustness guarantees, and automating teacher–student co-design for task-specific outputs.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression: Central, Context-Sensitive, and Best Used in Hybrid Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure across vision and NLP tasks and often recovers much of a teacher's performance, but it is not a universal cure: its reliability depends on what is distilled, how teachers and students are aligned, data availability, and complementary compression choices. Treating KD as a configurable, task-aware component within an integrated compression pipeline yields the most robust and deployable outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Aware Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing smaller, faster, or deployment‑specialized models by transferring information from larger teacher models. KD succeeds most reliably when treated as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline: practitioners should select appropriate transfer targets (logits, features, attention, relational signals), adapt objectives to student capacity and data regime, and combine distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies). While KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities, it is not a universal cure—limitations such as teacher imperfection, capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and the risk of propagating biases require targeted mitigations and careful evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical set of techniques for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models in deep learning and NLP. KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute, but its success depends on task-aware choices: what signals to transfer (logits, features, attention, relations), teacher–student alignment, available data (real, synthetic, or none), and complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Responsible and robust deployment further requires addressing distribution shift, low‑frequency or structured outputs, privacy and fairness concerns, and principled selection of distillation targets. I argue KD should be treated as a configurable toolkit — often essential for practical compression — rather than a turnkey solution; practitioners should select and combine distillation recipes according to capacity, data, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a configurable toolkit—selecting appropriate distillation signals, aligning teacher and student capacity, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or task-adaptive architecture search)—practitioners routinely obtain compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Success requires explicit attention to teacher quality, data availability or synthesis, optimization schedules, and safeguards against transferred biases or degraded rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis from Selected Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and deployment-ready students while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation techniques include matching logits (soft labels), feature- and layer-level imitation, ensemble and online schemes, data-free approaches, and task- or architecture-aware compression. Practical success depends on teacher quality and design, how and what information is transferred, availability and nature of data used for distillation, and how distillation is integrated with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Applications span NLP (BERT compression, reading comprehension, language generation), vision and generative models (GANs, lipreading, 3D detection), recommender systems, and graphs. Remaining challenges include aligning heterogeneous teacher-student architectures, preserving fine-grained or low-frequency behaviors, preventing transfer of teacher biases, and robust distillation under distribution shift or limited data.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Best Practices and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a broadly applicable and powerful approach for compressing models across modalities, but its effectiveness depends on design choices spanning what is distilled (logits, features, internal representations), how inputs are prepared (augmentation, sample selection), how multiple teachers are reconciled, and whether robustness or task-specific structure is considered. Recent work shows that combining soft-target regularization with feature- and intermediate-representation matching, careful input-side interventions, and adaptive distillation objectives yields the best tradeoffs between compression, accuracy, and robustness across vision, language, multimodal, graph, and generative-model settings.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multifaceted Toolbox for Compression and Responsible Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a versatile, task- and domain-adaptive toolbox rather than a single recipe. When combined with complementary mechanisms (feature and layer matching, many-to-many alignment, data augmentation, ensembling, pruning, quantization, and privacy-preserving protocols), KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving—or in some cases improving—task performance. Realizing these benefits reliably requires attention to what is distilled, how teacher and student are matched, and measures to mitigate risks such as teacher bias, data scarcity, and privacy concerns. Practical adoption should therefore treat KD as a configurable component of compression and deployment pipelines, with choices driven by the task, data availability, and safety constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide flexible, broadly applicable ways to transfer performance from large teacher models to compact student models so they can run under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. A diverse set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, relational signals) and procedures (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, meta-learned teachers, data-free synthesis) have been developed and integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search, ensembling). Empirical work across vision, language, speech, graphs, and recommendation systems shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can improve deployability, though success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and mitigation of transferred biases. Remaining directions include automated, task-adaptive transfer choices, robust data-free distillation, and principled controls for fairness and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Duran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Configurable Engine for Practical Model Compression — Powerful but Not Sufficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, practically proven approach for transferring capabilities from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce latency, memory use, and energy while preserving much of task performance. KD excels when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful teacher–student alignment, and appropriate data strategies; however, it is not a universal remedy. Reliable deployment requires treating KD as a configurable component of integrated compression pipelines with explicit provisions for teacher quality, data scarcity, distribution shift, and fairness or privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core set of techniques for producing compact models from larger teachers to enable deployment under constraints of compute, memory, latency, or privacy. Methods range from matching teacher logits to aligning internal features, attention maps, and layer correspondences; they are frequently combined with pruning, quantization, low-precision numerics, and architecture search. KD supports many practical settings — including data-limited, data-free, few-shot, federated, and cross-modal scenarios — but its effectiveness depends on choices such as which teacher signals to transfer, student capacity, data availability, and mitigation of transferred biases. Ongoing directions include principled theory for transfer objectives, robust and private distillation, and task-aware designs for structured outputs.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade‑offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring information from larger, more expensive teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD supports multiple transfer signals (soft labels, features, attention/relations, contrastive objectives) and modes (offline, online, multi‑teacher, data‑free), and is widely used across modalities including NLP, vision, recommender systems, GANs, and reinforcement learning. Practical deployment of KD hinges on choices about what to transfer, teacher and student design, data availability and augmentation, and mitigation of bias and distributional failures; combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment‑aware safeguards typically yields the best trade‑offs.

papers_seen.author: Hubbard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and widely adopted framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across modalities and tasks, a diverse set of transfer targets and training protocols has emerged — from matching soft logits to imitating intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive structures, and even using synthesized or privacy-aware pseudo-data. Best results typically come from combining multiple distilled signals, aligning teacher and student architectures (or adding projector layers), and integrating KD with complementary compression primitives and data strategies. Despite broad empirical success, persistent challenges include handling distribution shift and low-frequency behavior, aligning heterogeneous architectures, safeguarding privacy and fairness, and automating principled teacher selection. This synthesis condenses prevailing methods, empirical patterns, practical guidance, and open research directions documented in the supplied literature.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, practical family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD methods vary in their transfer targets and training protocols and are most effective when adapted to task, data, and student capacity. KD is powerful when integrated into a broader compression pipeline but has clear limits related to teacher–student capacity mismatch, data availability or mismatch, optimization difficulties, and the potential transfer of undesirable behaviors; these limits motivate careful design choices and complementary compression or mitigation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad toolbox for transferring predictive capacity from large, expensive models to smaller, faster, or privacy-preserving models. Methods range from soft-logit supervision to internal representation matching, contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical evidence across vision, NLP, graphs, and federated settings shows KD can recover much of a teacher's performance in resource-constrained deployments, while challenges remain in teacher selection, data availability, bias propagation, and task-specific design.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central, Configurable, but Insufficient — A Practical Position for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely used approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. As a practical tool it enables substantial efficiency gains across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks and supports privacy- and data-constrained settings. However, KD alone does not guarantee preservation of all important behaviors: success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher and student compatibility, data availability or synthesis, and integration with complementary compression methods. Therefore KD should be treated as a configurable core of an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline rather than as a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Foley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, First‑Line Tool — Powerful but Not Sufficient for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, flexible family of techniques that routinely enables compact, efficient models to inherit much of the behavior and performance of larger teacher models across vision, language, reinforcement learning, and healthcare applications. However, KD is context-sensitive: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality and alignment, student capacity and architecture, the data or synthetic-data strategy used for transfer, and explicit defenses against propagated biases or rare-case failures. The best practical outcomes treat KD as a configurable, task-aware core within an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation-level objectives, data strategies (including data-free or adversarial synthesis when needed), and complementary primitives such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Wells
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models to smaller, more deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD techniques—ranging from soft-logit matching to feature- and relation-level objectives, multi- and self-distillation, data-free or privacy-preserving protocols, and online/co-distillation schemes—enable substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute with modest accuracy loss when applied with task-aware design. Effective use of KD typically combines careful selection of what to transfer, attention to teacher–student capacity and data regimes, and integration with complementary compression mechanisms such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Remaining challenges include teacher imperfection and bias transfer, data scarcity and domain shift, capacity and optimization mismatch, and reliably distilling structured or generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods transfer predictive behavior or internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce memory, compute, and latency while retaining much of task performance. Methods span soft-target (logit) matching, representation- and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher and ensemble guidance, online and adversarial schemes, and data-free/zero-shot approaches. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a mechanism for knowledge transfer and as an implicit regularizer, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and augmentation, and the particular distillation objective. Practical deployments combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet resource, privacy, and latency constraints.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their performance. Across vision, language, graph, and generative modeling, KD methods vary by what is transferred (teacher logits, internal representations, attention, relational structure), how layers are aligned or projected, and how data constraints (limited access, privacy, or distribution shift) are handled. Empirical work demonstrates that combining output-level and representation-level objectives, using layer-mapping or projector modules, and adapting training data or curricula yields the best trade-offs between compactness and accuracy. Despite wide success, effective distillation requires careful choices about teacher quality, distilled signals, sample selection, and safeguards for robustness, privacy, and low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of the Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: This synthesis summarizes empirical findings, methodological variants, use-cases, limitations, and practical recommendations for knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques in deep learning and NLP. Drawing solely on the provided studies, it highlights common transfer targets and training regimes, domain- and task-specific adaptations, and recurring failure modes, and offers guidance on when and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods.
