However, KD also transfers teacher biases, faces optimization and data-distribution challenges, and requires careful choices of objectives, data augmentation, and teacher-student protocols to be effective in practice.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: The Efficacy and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into efficient students across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models, and reinforcement learning). Empirical work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance while offering substantial inference speedups and parameter reductions, and can be enhanced by targeted techniques (data augmentation, intermediate-layer matching, multi-teacher schedules, contrastive objectives, and meta-learning). However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends strongly on distillation procedure, data complexity, teacher–student alignment, and training dynamics. Practical deployment requires selecting distillation objectives and data strategies that address robustness, limited-data regimes, privacy/federation, and modality-specific needs.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, more efficient students while preserving predictive behavior and, in many cases, improving deployment properties such as latency, memory use, privacy, and robustness. The field has expanded from matching teacher logits to a broad set of signals and workflows — internal feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free generation, curriculum and selective-sample protocols, meta- and online-teaching schemes, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows that what to transfer (outputs vs. intermediate representations), how to align teacher and student (layer mapping, projectors), and which data to use (authentic, distilled, augmented, or synthetic) materially affect student outcomes. Practical deployments require task-aware design: align signals to student capacity, mitigate teacher error propagation, handle low-resource or privacy-constrained settings, and combine KD with complementary compression techniques. Remaining challenges include principled theory for which teacher signals are most informative across tasks, reliable transfer under data heterogeneity and domain shift, and preserving rare or structured outputs in sequence tasks.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, task-aware toolbox for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into compact student models. KD methods include output-level (soft logits) supervision, intermediate representation and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial or data-free sample generation, and online or multi‑teacher training. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which data to use or synthesize, KD routinely yields large reductions in parameter count and latency while preserving most of teacher performance. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: it is limited by teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and distribution shift, and risks such as propagated teacher biases and degraded rare-token or out‑of‑distribution behavior. Addressing these limits requires task-specific protocols, privacy‑ and robustness‑aware designs, and more principled, automated approaches to objective selection and layer alignment.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Analyses, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing and adapting large neural models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models while retaining much of their performance. A diverse set of KD approaches operate at the level of final outputs (logits), intermediate features, layer relations, or via adversarial and data-generation mechanisms. KD has been adapted across modalities and tasks — from NLP transformer compression to GAN and speech-model compression, cross-modal transfer, federated settings, and domain-specific applications — and interacts strongly with concerns about robustness, fairness, and transfer of inductive biases. Empirical and theoretical work has clarified when and why various KD variants help, and highlights open challenges in data heterogeneity, teacher-student mismatch, and automatic discovery of compact architectures.

papers_seen.author: Rowe
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. KD enables deployment under latency, memory, compute, and occasionally privacy constraints by matching teacher outputs, representations, or relational structure; it is routinely combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with data strategies (augmentation, synthetic data) to meet task- and deployment-specific requirements. While KD often preserves much of teacher performance, its success is context dependent and requires careful choices about distillation targets, teacher–student alignment, and data handling; open problems remain in principled target selection, robustness to distribution shift and rare outputs, and automated teacher–student matching.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression comprise a diverse set of techniques to produce smaller, faster, or more private models by transferring information from larger or auxiliary models. Research spans supervised teacher-student frameworks, self-distillation, multi-teacher and task-adaptive compression, and distillation combined with pruning, architecture search, adversarial training, and data augmentation. Practical work demonstrates benefits across vision, multimodal, graph, and NLP tasks, while theoretical analyses connect distillation to label smoothing, ensemble behavior, and bias–variance tradeoffs. Open challenges include aligning heterogeneous inputs and modalities, preserving robustness and privacy, and handling low-resource or low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques reduce model size and inference cost by transferring information from larger, more expensive models (teachers) to smaller, cheaper models (students). Across modalities and tasks, researchers have developed logit- and feature-level distillation, layer-wise and many-to-many layer matching, task-aware filtering, projector-based adapters, meta-learned teachers, multi-teacher weighting, and data- or privacy-constrained workflows. Empirical work demonstrates that carefully designed distillation protocols can retain much of teacher performance (and sometimes improve generalization) while enabling deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy; theoretical analyses offer insight into when soft labels help and when hard labels are necessary. Remaining challenges include bridging capacity gaps, dealing with mismatched architectures and modalities, operating without original data, and guaranteeing privacy under compression.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Mechanisms, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically effective family of techniques that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or auxiliary models into smaller, deployable students. KD supports many transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and training protocols (offline teacher, online mutual learning, self-distillation, multi-teacher and teacher-free schemes) and can be integrated with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. When carefully designed, KD not only approximates teacher performance but can act as a regularizer that improves generalization; however, reliable outcomes require attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data selection, layer alignment, and privacy or domain constraints.

papers_seen.author: Garner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Context‑Dependent Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of methods for producing compact models by transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teachers to smaller students. Empirically, KD enables substantial reductions in compute, memory, and latency while often preserving much of teacher performance across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks. However, KD is not automatic: its success depends on deliberate choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and integration with complementary compression and robustness measures. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a core, configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone silver bullet.

papers_seen.author: Schmidt
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact students. A large and consistent body of work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance across modalities when the distilled signals, data strategy, and teacher–student alignment are chosen carefully. At the same time, KD’s effectiveness is context-dependent: it is bounded by data availability, teacher quality, capacity mismatch, and risks of transferring undesirable behaviors, so it is best applied as part of an integrated compression pipeline that includes complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), data strategies, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Beyond in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a compression trick into a broad set of techniques that enable efficient deployment, cross-modal transfer, federated and privacy-preserving learning, and improved generalization across domains. Empirical results across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs) show that KD can substantially reduce model size and latency while retaining most of the teacher performance. However, the success of KD depends on careful choices — teacher quality, what to distill (outputs, features, internal representations), data availability and augmentation, and the loss or alignment mechanism — and recent work proposes multiple refinements (multi-teacher schemes, adversarial critics, projector modules, teacher-free variants) that mitigate known failure modes. The balance of empirical evidence and theoretical analyses indicates that KD is both practically indispensable for many compression tasks and a fertile area for research on how knowledge should be measured, transferred, and regularized.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Tool: Integrating Distillation with Representation, Data, and Architecture Strategies for Robust Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and broadly applicable approach for producing smaller, more deployable models from large teachers in deep learning and NLP. However, KD alone is rarely sufficient to meet real-world deployment constraints: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of distilled signals (logits, features, attention), and access to or synthesis of suitable training data. Best results arise when KD is embedded in an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation-level matching, projector or layer-mapping modules, data and curriculum strategies, and architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, or layer skipping). Careful attention to optimization, robustness, privacy, and low-frequency behaviors is required to avoid propagating teacher errors and to produce reliable compact models for downstream applications.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied set of techniques for producing compact student models from larger teacher ensembles or single models. The literature shows a rich taxonomy of distillation signals (soft logits, feature- and attention-level targets, relational/contrastive objectives), protocols (offline, online, multi-teacher, self- or co-distillation), and engineering integrations (projector adapters, curriculum or confidence-weighting, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, and cross-modal tasks indicates that carefully designed KD pipelines can recover a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and deployment cost; however, practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and mitigating failure modes such as transferred biases, degraded rare-output behavior, and capacity mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Practical Power, Limits, and Responsible Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and empirically validated family of techniques for compressing, adapting, and deploying deep models in constrained or sensitive settings. KD transfers information from one or more teacher models to smaller or otherwise constrained students via soft targets, intermediate-representation matching, contrastive/objective-level alignment, adversarial schemes, or synthetic-data generation. When designed carefully—choosing suitable teacher signals, aligning teacher and student capacity, integrating augmentation and complementary compression methods, and accounting for domain shift and fairness—KD routinely recovers most of a teacher's performance while enabling lower latency, smaller memory footprints, and new deployment modes (edge, federated, privacy-sensitive). However, KD is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher–student mismatch, optimization choices, and the potential transfer of undesirable properties (bias, rare-token degradation). Responsible use requires principled teacher selection, careful objective design, augmentation and sample-selection strategies, and techniques for data-free or privacy-preserving scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, flexible approach for producing compact models from larger teachers that preserves much of their performance across tasks and modalities. Its strengths arise from multiple transfer mechanisms (logits, intermediate features, attention, relational signals) and from compatibility with complementary compression tools. However, KD is not automatic: success requires careful choices about what to transfer, teacher quality, student capacity, data strategies, and integration with other compression methods. I argue that KD should be treated as a first-class, configurable component of modern model-deployment toolkits, with explicit practices to mitigate its failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Rodgers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applied framework for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger teachers to compact students. Across vision, language, speech, graphs, and generative tasks, KD variants—ranging from soft-logit matching to intermediate-representation, attention, relational, and contrastive objectives, as well as adversarial, data-free, online, and multi‑teacher protocols—have been adapted to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, compute, privacy, and domain adaptation). Empirical work shows KD can recover a substantial fraction of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, signal choice, data strategy, and architecture alignment are addressed; however, KD is not a universal cure and must be integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and safeguards for bias, low‑frequency phenomena, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, more expensive models (teachers) to smaller, cheaper models (students) to reduce inference cost, enable deployment on constrained devices, and support privacy- or resource-constrained settings. Approaches span soft-label distillation, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, data-free and zero-shot methods, multi-teacher and ensemble distillation, self-distillation, task- and modality-specific objectives, and combinations with pruning. Empirical work across vision, speech, 3D detection, recommender systems, and multiple NLP tasks demonstrates that carefully designed distillation strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while significantly reducing latency and memory. The literature also provides growing theoretical insight into when and how distillation helps, and identifies open challenges including imperfect teachers, domain shift, low-frequency token fidelity, modality mismatch, and heterogeneous-device federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad toolbox for transferring predictive capacity from large, expensive models to smaller, faster, or privacy-preserving models. Methods range from soft-logit supervision to internal representation matching, contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical evidence across vision, NLP, graphs, and federated settings shows KD can recover much of a teacher's performance in resource-constrained deployments, while challenges remain in teacher selection, data availability, bias propagation, and task-specific design.

papers_seen.author: Alexander
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical approach for producing smaller, faster, and deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact students. KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory use, and communication cost while often preserving much of teacher performance across modalities. However, its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of transferred undesirable behaviors. For robust, real-world deployment KD should be used as the core of an integrated compression pipeline that includes complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), targeted data strategies, and safeguards for privacy, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broad family of techniques for compressing large or expensive models into smaller, faster, or more deployable ones by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Methods differ in the form of transferred knowledge (soft logits, hidden features, contrastive distributions, synthetic data, or cross-modal alignments), in how and when distillation is applied (offline, online, layer-wise, task-adaptive, or data-free), and in the problems they target (classification, detection, generation, language tasks, graph learning, or novel-view synthesis). Empirical work demonstrates that appropriate choices about teacher signals, data manipulation, and architectural search can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities; theoretical work begins to clarify when soft labels help and when hard labels or mixed supervision are needed. Remaining challenges include optimization gaps between teacher and student, dataset and fairness concerns, and scaling distillation reliably in large distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Wolf
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Central, Practical, but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and widely used family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD methods have expanded from simple logits-matching to include feature- and layer-level imitation, self-distillation, data-free and federated protocols, and many-to-many teacher–student mappings. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD regularly yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and data availability or synthesis. KD is best treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, augmentation, or synthetic-data strategies—rather than as a standalone panacea.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Effectiveness, Limitations, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible method for compressing large models into smaller, faster, and often more interpretable models across vision, language, speech, and recommendation systems. KD works both as a stand-alone compression technique and as a complementary tool that combines well with pruning, quantization, multi-teacher strategies, and privacy-aware or federated settings. While highly effective in practice, KD has limits—especially around data availability, heterogeneity, and theoretical understanding—that recent work addresses with data-free methods, meta-learning teachers, and principled analyses.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven approach for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models to smaller student models. KD methods include logits matching, intermediate feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, and variants that operate online, with multiple teachers, or without access to original training data. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component within a broader compression pipeline that also uses pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies; its benefits and limits depend on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful mitigation of bias and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Thompson

papers_seen.author: Wang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfers information from larger or composite teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, enable deployment under resource or privacy constraints, and sometimes improve generalization. papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of the Provided Literature
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under constraints of latency, memory, compute, or privacy. KD has enabled strong empirical gains across modalities and tasks (classification, generation, translation, graph learning, and recommender systems) but requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate transfer of undesirable behaviors. Key practical themes include selecting appropriate distillation signals, handling teacher–student capacity and architecture mismatches, designing or synthesizing data when originals are unavailable, and integrating KD with complementary compression methods to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques form a diverse set of methods for producing smaller, faster, or more deployable models by transferring knowledge from larger or specialized models. KD is used across domains—image classification, detection (2D and 3D), recommendation/CTR, language model compression, federated and heterogeneous-device learning, and reinforcement learning—and is frequently combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or curriculum strategies. Recent work examines theoretical aspects (e.g., bias–variance tradeoffs and statistical interactions with data augmentation), practical design choices (teacher-student layer alignment, many-to-many mappings, ensemble teachers), and extensions that address privacy, fairness, and low-data regimes. Despite strong empirical success, open problems remain in understanding when particular KD variants best transfer generalization, how to measure and mitigate transferred biases, and how to optimally combine KD with other compression primitives for different constraints.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Findings, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller student models. KD encompasses a range of transfer targets and training protocols and is commonly combined with complementary compression methods to meet deployment constraints. Practical success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis strategies, and careful choice of distilled signals and training procedures.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context-Dependent Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a pragmatic pathway to compress large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate representations. Empirical work across vision, speech, language, multimodal and graph domains shows KD can retain much of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in parameters, latency, and memory when combined with complementary compression tools. However, real-world success requires careful choice of teacher signals, data strategies, and optimization protocols to address capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and modality or deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary, Configurable Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains. KD supports multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals), diverse scheduling regimes (offline, online, progressive), and synergistic combination with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). While KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest loss in task performance, its success is context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity, data availability (or synthetic/data-free strategies), and explicit measures to mitigate bias, robustness, and privacy concerns determine outcomes. Consequently, KD should be treated as a first-order, configurable tool in compression pipelines—selected and tuned according to task, data, and deployment constraints—rather than a one-size-fits-all recipe.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Olson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated family of techniques for transferring information from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD supports a wide set of transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention and relational signals), training protocols (offline, online/self‑distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free and few‑shot), and complementary compression mechanisms (pruning, quantization, architecture search). While KD routinely produces strong efficiency–accuracy trade‑offs across modalities, its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and careful selection of what and how to transfer; practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable component within larger compression pipelines and pair it with task‑aware safeguards for robustness, privacy, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. Approaches vary by what is transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention maps, channel statistics, or decision-boundary information), by whether original training data are available, and by whether the goal is efficiency, robustness, privacy, or domain adaptation. Empirical work across vision, multimodal, speech, and natural language tasks shows that careful choices of transfer targets, loss formulations, teacher ensembles, and training schedules can yield compact models that approach — and in some cases match or exceed — teacher performance while enabling deployment under resource, latency, privacy, or domain constraints. Remaining challenges include optimization difficulties that prevent perfect belief matching, distribution-shift and heterogeneity issues in federated or data-free settings, and trade-offs among accuracy, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, efficient student models to reduce latency, memory, and deployment cost while often preserving much of the original performance. A broad toolkit has been developed—logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and channel-wise objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search—that is applied across vision, language, graphs, reinforcement learning, and generative modeling. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD is effective in many settings but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful objective and alignment choices; practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable component of a larger compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a broad family of techniques that transfer information from larger, often multi-source or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. Across vision, language, speech, multimodal and generative settings, KD has evolved beyond simple logit matching to include representation- and relation-level objectives, adversarial or data-free generation, online and self-distillation protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization and architecture search. These approaches routinely enable large reductions in inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance, but reliable deployment requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data. Important open directions remain in principled theory, robust distillation under heterogenous and low-data regimes, and preserving long-tail or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger (or specialized) teacher models to smaller, faster, or more deployable student models. KD methods vary in what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational/contrastive structure), how mappings between teacher and student are implemented (layer alignment, projectors, many-to-many mappings), and how training is scheduled (fixed teacher, student-friendly teacher learning, meta-learning, or self-distillation). KD is frequently combined with other compression primitives (pruning, quantization, low-precision numerics, progressive module replacement, and architecture search) and with data strategies (augmentation, mixup, data-free synthesis, domain adaptation) to meet deployment, privacy, and domain-shift constraints. While KD often yields strong empirical gains in accuracy, efficiency, and robustness, its success depends on teacher quality, the distilled signals chosen, data availability and complexity, and careful optimization; open problems remain in principled selection of distillation targets, mitigating transferred biases, and integrating KD optimally with other compression tools.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central, Context‑Sensitive, and Best Used as Part of an Integrated Compression Pipeline
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely effective toolkit for producing compact models from larger teachers across vision, language, speech, and graph domains. Empirical evidence shows KD can reduce model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance, but success depends on what signals are transferred, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and the training protocol. I argue KD should be treated as a central but context‑sensitive component of compression pipelines and combined with representation, data, and architecture strategies to reliably meet deployment goals.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and highly practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD techniques range from simple soft-target matching to representation- and task-aware objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-augmentation and data-free protocols, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is effective across modalities and tasks but is not a silver bullet: its success depends on teacher quality, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and augmentation, architecture alignment, and explicit handling of biases and distribution shift. Treated as a core component within an integrated compression pipeline and designed with task constraints in mind, KD yields reliable tradeoffs between efficiency and fidelity for deployment in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applied approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD methods span soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and data‑free or online protocols. Empirical work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and mitigation of bias and distribution-shift risks. Effective deployment treats KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and careful data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Versatile, and Context‑Dependent for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across modalities. KD provides a flexible set of transfer signals and training protocols that enable substantial efficiency gains when paired with appropriate data strategies and complementary compression primitives. However, KD is context‑dependent: its effectiveness hinges on teacher–student alignment, data regime, and targeted safeguards against bias and distributional mismatch, so it should be applied as a configurable component within broader compression and deployment pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and communication while often preserving much of task performance. KD is a flexible family of techniques that operate at output, representation, relational, or decision-boundary levels and is commonly combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and alignment, and careful design of objectives and training pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Bautista
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted technique for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD supports many transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals), training protocols (offline, online, multi‑teacher, data‑free/self‑distillation), and is effective across modalities. However, its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful choice of what and how to transfer. For reliable deployment, KD should be treated as a configurable element within integrated, task‑aware compression pipelines that combine distillation with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies) and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically validated framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, graph, and generative tasks. KD supports multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational and contrastive signals), can operate in multi-teacher and data-free settings, and integrates with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data strategy (including synthetic or public data when originals are unavailable), and task-aware objective design. KD has documented failure modes — e.g., propagation of teacher errors or biases, difficulty preserving low-frequency phenomena, and distributional mismatch — which motivate targeted remedies such as multi-signal objectives, teacher scheduling, meta-learned teachers, and joint optimization with other compression tools. Treated as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline rather than a single recipe, KD is an essential practical tool for model deployment under resource, privacy, and latency constraints.

papers_seen.author: Reynolds
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile family of techniques that enables deployment of large neural models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure into smaller, faster students. Across vision, language, and other modalities, KD variants and hybrids often deliver substantial efficiency and deployment gains when combined with task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to schedule transfer, and which complementary compression tools to use. However, KD is context‑sensitive: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and explicit mitigation of transferred errors or low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as Central but Insufficient: A Task‑Aware, Pipeline‑Centric Position for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, broadly applicable set of techniques that reliably reduces inference cost by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller student models. Empirical evidence across vision, language, multimodal, and speech tasks shows that carefully designed KD pipelines often recover most of teacher performance — and in some circumstances can even improve student generalization — but consistent success requires task‑aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. I argue KD should be treated as the default, central component of model‑compression workflows while being explicitly integrated into broader, deployment‑aware pipelines that address teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, fairness/privacy risks, and hardware constraints.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Empirical evidence across vision and language shows KD can substantially reduce inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but its success depends on careful choices about what information is transferred, how teachers and students are aligned, and how distillation is combined with complementary compression methods. I argue KD should be treated as the central element of an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a sole solution.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger, often over-parameterized teacher models into smaller, efficient student models. Over the past decade these techniques have diversified from simple logit-matching to a broad set of objectives and pipelines — including feature- and representation-matching, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial procedures, data-free and privacy-aware methods, multi-teacher schemes, teacher design, and selective sample strategies. KD has been applied across domains (NLP, vision, graph learning, generative models, novel-view synthesis, speech, and recommender systems), producing substantial reductions in parameters and latency while retaining or sometimes improving downstream performance. The literature highlights important practical trade-offs (utility vs. fairness, robustness, data availability, and teacher–student mismatch), and suggests promising directions in adaptive teacher design, rigorous uncertainty and fairness controls, and domain- and task-specific distillation objectives.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When designed around task objectives, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and deployment constraints—and when combined with complementary compression primitives—KD routinely reduces inference cost, memory footprint, and communication overhead while preserving much of teacher performance. Yet KD is not automatic: it requires careful choices about distillation signals, architecture alignment, data strategies (including data‑free or synthetic data when originals are unavailable), and safeguards to avoid propagating teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, task-aware family of methods for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD uses a variety of transfer targets and training protocols to reduce inference cost, enable deployment under memory and latency constraints, and—when carefully applied—preserve much of teacher performance. Practical application treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline, combining distillation with architecture design, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Moon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers. When treated as a configurable component of a compression pipeline and adapted to teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of a teacher's performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. However, KD is not a turnkey cure: it must be combined with projector or layer-mapping techniques, ensemble and adversarial strategies where appropriate, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) while explicitly mitigating failure modes such as bias transfer, low-frequency degradation, and data scarcity. Continued theoretical and empirical work is needed to standardize best practices, automate signal selection, and robustly distill structured or generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Dougherty
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task‑Aware Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically effective approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD works at multiple levels (soft targets, intermediate representations, relational/contrastive signals, and data‑synthesis protocols) and is most reliable when adapted to task constraints, teacher and student capacity, and available data. I argue that KD should be treated as the central, configurable core of any compression pipeline but not as a standalone cure: to be robust and production‑ready it must be combined with complementary compression primitives, careful layer and signal design, and specific remedies for documented failure modes such as teacher–student mismatch, transferred biases, and degradation on low‑frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Fuller
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, more deployable student models. The literature converges on a taxonomy of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational/contrastive signals), protocols (offline teacher–student, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data‑free/synthetic data), and engineering integrations (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, pretraining, and data strategies). Empirical work shows KD often preserves a substantial portion of teacher performance while substantially reducing parameters, latency, and memory across vision, language, speech, recommendation, and multimodal applications, but success is context dependent: it hinges on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of transferred biases or robustness failures. Current open problems include principled theory of what transfers, reliable distillation under distribution shift or privacy constraints, and preserving low-frequency or structured outputs in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Open Problems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. Across modalities and tasks, a diverse toolkit — including logits/soft-target matching, feature- and relation-level objectives, multi- and self-distillation, online and data-free protocols, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design — has been shown to deliver large efficiency gains with modest performance loss when applied with task-aware engineering. Important remaining challenges include theoretical understanding of what is transferred, robust and private distillation under data scarcity or distribution shift, and reliably preserving fine-grained or structured behaviors.
