papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical Tool that Requires Task-Aware, Complementary Engineering
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile strategy for producing compact models from large teachers that supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD reliably reduces inference cost while often preserving most of a teacher's performance, but its success depends on matching distillation objectives and procedures to task constraints and student capacity. Best outcomes arise when KD is treated as part of an integrated compression pipeline that includes representation alignment, data- and task-aware strategies, and complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable Tool for Model Compression with Practical Caveats
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable, empirically validated family of techniques that enables production of compact, efficient models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller students. KD succeeds across modalities and tasks when its objectives, data, and teacher-student design are matched to deployment constraints, but it is not a turnkey remedy: careful method selection and safeguards are required to avoid capacity mismatch, optimization failure modes, and transfer of undesirable behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster students to enable deployment under constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and compute. A diverse set of distillation targets and training paradigms—soft-label (logit) matching, intermediate feature and attention-map imitation, layer-wise mapping, adversarial and data-free generation of surrogate examples, online and multi-teacher schemes, self-distillation, and integration with architecture search or pruning—have been developed and adapted to vision, language, multimodal, and generative tasks. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most of the teacher's accuracy (and in some settings improves generalization or robustness) when combined with task-aware choices of signals to transfer, data augmentation, and teacher-student design; remaining gaps and failure modes are linked to teacher quality, data availability and distribution shift, heterogeneous architectures, and fairness or robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. Approaches vary by what is transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention maps, channel statistics, or decision-boundary information), by whether original training data are available, and by whether the goal is efficiency, robustness, privacy, or domain adaptation. Empirical work across vision, multimodal, speech, and natural language tasks shows that careful choices of transfer targets, loss formulations, teacher ensembles, and training schedules can yield compact models that approach — and in some cases match or exceed — teacher performance while enabling deployment under resource, latency, privacy, or domain constraints. Remaining challenges include optimization difficulties that prevent perfect belief matching, distribution-shift and heterogeneity issues in federated or data-free settings, and trade-offs among accuracy, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Insufficient Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and broadly effective family of techniques for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teachers' performance. Empirical results across vision, language, ranking, detection, translation, federated settings, and reinforcement learning show KD reduces parameters and latency, can improve generalization, and enables domain- and privacy-aware workflows. At the same time, KD has important failure modes—dependence on distillation data and teacher–student alignment, capability mismatches, and transfer of teacher errors or biases—that require targeted solutions. Best practice is to treat KD as a central component of an integrated compression pipeline, combined with representation-level matching, data strategies, architecture-aware transformations, and privacy- or domain-specific adaptations.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Configurable Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller students that can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD supports a wide range of transfer targets and training regimes and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design choices. However, KD is context-dependent: its success requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and explicit mitigation of risks such as bias transfer and distribution-shift degradation.

papers_seen.author: Cooke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision, language, speech, detection, recommendation, and multimodal tasks, KD methods—ranging from soft-logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, adversarial and contrastive objectives, data-free synthesis, and online or multi-teacher protocols—enable substantial efficiency gains while often preserving much of teacher performance. Success depends on choices about what to transfer, data strategy, teacher–student alignment, and complementary compression (e.g., pruning, quantization, or architecture search). Practical deployments use task-aware adaptations, confidence- or curriculum-based weighting, and privacy- or federated-aware designs; remaining challenges include teacher–student mismatch, limited or private data, distribution shift, rare-output transfer, and principled theory for optimal transfer.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Central, but Contextual Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-ready approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster, or more deployable students. When combined with complementary compression primitives, careful choice of distillation targets and protocols, and task- or data-aware design, KD routinely produces compact models that retain a large fraction of teacher performance. However, KD is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability or synthesis strategy, and attention to robustness, low-frequency phenomena, and distribution shift. Best practice treats KD as a flexible toolkit that must be adapted to deployment constraints and complemented with privacy-, fairness-, and robustness-aware methods.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers across vision, language, graph, recommendation, and generative settings. KD encompasses a range of techniques—soft-target matching, intermediate feature and attention alignment, contrastive and adversarial objectives, layer- and channel-wise mappings, and data- or task-aware variants—and is frequently combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can enable deployable, lower-latency models, improve robustness and interpretability in some settings, and serve as a substrate for domain adaptation and privacy-aware workflows; its success depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, data availability (including data-free or few-shot regimes), and practical engineering choices.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Indispensable but Task‑Aware
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable family of methods for compressing large models into smaller, faster, or more deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD variants have been successfully adapted across modalities and tasks, and when designed with awareness of task constraints, data availability, and student capacity, distillation yields substantial practical gains. However, KD has concrete limits—capacity mismatch, data scarcity, bias propagation, and failures on rare phenomena—that make it most effective when integrated into broader, task‑aware compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression methods aim to transfer behavior and representations from larger, more expensive models into smaller, efficient ones while retaining task performance. Across modalities and tasks, research has developed many complementary mechanisms — soft-label mimicry, intermediate representation matching, teacher-student curriculum designs, self-distillation, multi-teacher and online schemes, data- or generator-based transfer, and domain- or modality-specific adaptations — to balance accuracy, latency, and resource constraints. Empirical work shows that properly designed distillation can recover most teacher performance (and in some settings even surpass it) while enabling deployment on constrained hardware and improving reproducibility and privacy. Success depends on the distillation targets, the teacher-student pairing and training regime, the use of auxiliary data or synthetic examples, and task-specific modifications.

papers_seen.author: Mcintyre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models so they run under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational/contrastive structures, adversarial or data-free synthesis) and are routinely combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and multilingual tasks shows that properly designed distillation pipelines often recover a large fraction of teacher performance, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and alignment, data availability or synthesis, and careful choice of objectives and layer mappings. Important open problems include robust data-free distillation, principled transfer choices for heterogeneous architectures, and controls for fairness and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Task-Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single recipe but as a versatile, task-aware toolkit that enables compact, efficient, and deployable models across modalities. KD methods—ranging from logit-based soft targets to feature-, layer-, and relation-level matching, and including self-, multi-teacher, data-free, and online variants—consistently trade small accuracy loss for large gains in latency, memory, and privacy. Reliable application requires careful attention to teacher quality and compatibility, what to transfer, the data regime, and interactions with regularizers and complementary compression methods. When designed around deployment constraints and task objectives, KD delivers practical, often substantial improvements for on-device inference, domain adaptation, federated settings, and robustness-sensitive applications.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Configurable Component for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD supports multiple transfer targets and training protocols, interoperates with complementary compression techniques, and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its effectiveness is context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and distribution shift determine outcomes, so KD should be applied as a task- and deployment-aware component within integrated compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Salinas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, diverse family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large or composite teacher models into smaller, faster, or more deployable student models. The field has evolved from matching soft output probabilities to include feature- and layer-level imitation, attention and relational transfer, contrastive and adversarial objectives, data-free and privacy-preserving protocols, and online or multi-teacher schemes. KD is effective across modalities and tasks (vision, NLP, speech, graphs, and multimodal systems) and often forms part of a broader compression pipeline together with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, KD success depends on task-aware choices—teacher quality, student capacity, the distillation signal, and the data available—and several practical challenges remain, including distribution shift, data heterogeneity (especially in federated settings), low-frequency/rare-token behavior, and the risk of transferring teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Manning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Practical, but Insufficient — A Position and Recommended Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely adopted framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. Empirical evidence across vision and language shows that KD can reduce inference cost, latency, and memory requirements and enable deployment under privacy, communication, and resource constraints. However, KD alone does not guarantee robust, unbiased, or optimal compressed models: failures arise from teacher–student mismatch, limited or absent data, transfer of teacher errors and biases, poor handling of low-frequency phenomena, and vulnerability under distribution shift or adversarial attack. Practical compression therefore treats KD as a core component within an integrated pipeline—combining representation-aware objectives, curriculum and sample-selection strategies, adversarial or synthetic-data generation for data-scarce regimes, and complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to realize reliable, resource-aware students.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practically essential family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models by transferring information from larger teacher models. Across vision, language, graphs, recommendation, and federated settings, KD variants transfer soft logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, contrastive signals, synthetic inputs, or ensemble outputs. KD can enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, improve student generalization, support privacy-preserving workflows, and interact fruitfully with pruning and low-precision numerics. However, the benefits depend strongly on data availability, teacher quality, architecture alignment, and training protocols; important failure modes include optimization gaps, preserved or amplified teacher biases, degraded rare-token behavior, and teacher inference cost. The literature provides many practical strategies—feature- and layer-wise matching, multi- and self-distillation, adversarial or data-free sample generation, student-aware teacher design, and hardware-aware co-design—to mitigate these limitations and extend KD to specialized tasks such as federated learning, continual/lifelong learning, graph neural networks, recommendation systems, and cross-modal transfer.

papers_seen.author: Weeks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Central, Practical, but Context-Sensitive Strategy for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practically essential set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students. KD enables deployment under strict latency, memory, and privacy constraints and supports cross-modal and domain transfer. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability and privacy, and complementary compression and training practices. Reliable compression treats distillation as a core component of a broader, task-aware pipeline rather than a standalone recipe.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Hoover
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Context‑Sensitive, and Best‑Practice Driven
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically essential tool for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers across modalities. When integrated with complementary compression techniques and adapted to the data and deployment constraints, KD routinely yields students that recover a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and inference cost. However, KD is not a universal solution: its effectiveness depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of transferred signals, and the availability or synthesis of suitable data. Responsible application requires explicit mitigation of failure modes such as propagated teacher errors, degraded modeling of rare phenomena, distribution shift, and privacy risks. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline and provides practical recommendations for when and how to apply KD effectively in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Lucas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary, Context‑Aware Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically proven approach for producing compact, efficient models from large teachers. KD routinely achieves large reductions in inference cost and model size while recovering much of teacher performance, and it enables domain, modality, and privacy‑aware adaptations. However, KD is not a turnkey cure: its reliability depends on careful choices of what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and data strategy, and it should be applied as the core element of a broader, deployment‑aware compression portfolio that includes pruning, quantization, architecture search, and targeted data interventions.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models to reduce latency, memory, and compute while retaining much of teacher performance. A diverse set of distillation targets and training protocols has been developed (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational/contrastive signals; offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, and data‑free variants). Empirical work across vision, language, speech and multimodal tasks shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and when training/data procedures are adapted to task and deployment constraints. Remaining gaps include principled layer alignment across heterogeneous architectures, robust distillation under limited or private data, preservation of long‑tail/low‑frequency behaviors, and theoretical understanding of when particular teacher signals are necessary.

papers_seen.author: Dalton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Configurable Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible approach that reliably reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. KD works via multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational signals) and training protocols (offline, online, multi‑teacher, adversarial, data‑free). Its practical value comes from being a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies—rather than a single, automatic cure‑all. Realizing KD's benefits requires careful choices about teacher selection, student capacity and architecture, distilled signals, training data, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies have become central to deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained settings. Across vision, multimodal, and language domains, researchers have developed approaches that transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller students via logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or adversarial objectives. Work spans supervised and unsupervised settings, data-free or black-box scenarios, continual and federated use-cases, and concerns such as privacy and adversarial robustness. Practical recipes combine distillation with pruning, structured sparsity, progressive module replacement, and many-to-many layer mapping to balance accuracy, latency, and memory. Open challenges remain in data- and domain-limited regimes, robust and private compression, and principled selection of which teacher knowledge to transfer for a given downstream task.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Findings, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller, efficient student models to meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Over the past decade, KD methods have evolved from simple soft-target (logit) matching to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi‑teacher and online regimes, and data‑free or adversarial synthesis. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can preserve much of a teacher’s performance and in many cases improve generalization, but practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of signals to transfer, and the availability and match of distillation data; reliable deployment therefore treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that combines representation-aware objectives, data and curriculum strategies, and complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Steele
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, more efficient student models to reduce inference cost, memory use, and communication while preserving task performance. Practitioners apply KD across modalities—vision, language, speech, and multimodal settings—using a variety of targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals) and training protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi‑teacher, curriculum schedules, and data-free/few-shot variants). KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when its design is matched to teacher quality, student capacity, and data availability. Remaining gaps include reliable transfer of robustness and long‑tail behaviors, principled teacher–student co‑design, and data- and privacy-constrained distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Thomas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Contextual Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across modalities. Empirical and methodological work shows KD frequently preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and inference cost. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architectural alignment, data availability and design, and explicit mitigation of transferred errors, biases, and rare-case degradation. For robust, production-ready compression pipelines, KD should be treated as the central mechanism embedded within task-aware practices that include complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful teacher–student engineering, and data- and fairness-aware protocols.

papers_seen.author: Flores
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise specialized students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, researchers have extended KD beyond soft-label matching to include feature- and attention-level alignment, contrastive and relational objectives, online and self-distillation, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols. Practical success depends on teacher quality and student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, data availability or synthetic-data strategies, and combinations with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Remaining challenges include principled understanding of when particular signals help, handling heterogeneous or non-iid data in federated settings, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and reliably scaling distillation in large distributed systems.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across modalities and tasks. Modern KD methods span simple soft-target matching to representation-, attention-, and relation-level transfer, and they are routinely combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware training protocols. Empirical work shows KD can yield large efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss when teacher quality, student capacity, data, and transfer signals are carefully aligned; open problems include theory, robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare-token behavior, privacy, and principled automation of teacher–student alignment.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central tools for shrinking model size and latency while preserving performance across computer vision, natural language processing, recommendation, and federated settings. Research has expanded beyond the original logits-matching paradigm into feature mimicking, many-to-many layer mapping, teacher engineering, multi-teacher schemes, data- and privacy-constrained distillation, and task-adaptive compression. Empirical and theoretical work highlights important interactions between data complexity, teacher strength, inductive bias, and augmentation strategies, and identifies practical challenges including model-heterogeneity, data heterogeneity, and the need for robust data-free methods. The field increasingly emphasizes not only how to distill but also what to distill (logits, features, inter-class relations, view- or task-specific knowledge) and how to adapt distillation to application constraints (privacy, federated settings, domain shifts, resource budgets).

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression techniques form a broad, practical toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. The literature shows that appropriately chosen distillation signals, teacher–student design, and data strategies allow compact models to recover much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and deployment cost. Practical pipelines commonly combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search, and adapt to constraints such as privacy, heterogeneous devices, and limited or unlabeled data. Despite widespread empirical success, important limitations persist—teacher bias transfer, capacity mismatch, degraded rare-output behavior, and theoretical gaps linking distillation signals to student generalization—motivating ongoing work in adaptive teacher selection, data-free distillation, and task-aware compression design.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Insights, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques reduce the size and computational cost of large deep models while retaining much of their performance. Across classification, sequence modeling, generation, and structured prediction, researchers have developed soft-label distillation, intermediate-feature guidance, adversarial and contrastive objectives, projector and embedding modules, and privacy-aware mechanisms to transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller students. Empirical and theoretical work highlights trade-offs among bias, variance, teacher quality, and data complexity, and shows that distillation interacts with pre-training, label smoothing, and modality differences. Applications span speech and machine translation to GANs and graph neural networks; complementary methods such as pruning and block-structured compression can further improve deployment on constrained hardware.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applied approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD methods span soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and data‑free or online protocols. Empirical work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and mitigation of bias and distribution-shift risks. Effective deployment treats KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and careful data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Salinas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, diverse family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large or composite teacher models into smaller, faster, or more deployable student models. The field has evolved from matching soft output probabilities to include feature- and layer-level imitation, attention and relational transfer, contrastive and adversarial objectives, data-free and privacy-preserving protocols, and online or multi-teacher schemes. KD is effective across modalities and tasks (vision, NLP, speech, graphs, and multimodal systems) and often forms part of a broader compression pipeline together with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, KD success depends on task-aware choices—teacher quality, student capacity, the distillation signal, and the data available—and several practical challenges remain, including distribution shift, data heterogeneity (especially in federated settings), low-frequency/rare-token behavior, and the risk of transferring teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for transferring behavior and representations from large teacher models into smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while often preserving most of a teacher's performance. Its practical value emerges when KD is used as a configurable core within integrated compression pipelines that also employ pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies. At the same time, KD is not sufficient by itself: success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of distillation signals, and careful handling of data, bias, and distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical strategy for compressing large models into smaller, faster students for deployment across vision, language, multimodal, and graph tasks. When combined with architecture-aware design, layer- and feature-level objectives, adversarial or relational losses, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, NAS), KD enables substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss and can sometimes improve generalization. KD also faces clear limits—teacher bias, capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and optimization instability—that require task-aware curricula, multi-teacher or ensemble strategies, and careful selection of distilled signals. This paper argues that KD should be the first-line instrument in compression toolkits for deep learning and NLP, provided practitioners adopt principled protocols that address known failure modes and integrate KD with complementary methods for the target deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically proven approach for producing compact, efficient models from large teachers. KD routinely achieves large reductions in inference cost and model size while recovering much of teacher performance, and it enables domain, modality, and privacy‑aware adaptations. However, KD is not a turnkey cure: its reliability depends on careful choices of what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and data strategy, and it should be applied as the core element of a broader, deployment‑aware compression portfolio that includes pruning, quantization, architecture search, and targeted data interventions.

papers_seen.author: Cain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a flexible set of methods for transferring information from larger or more expressive teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. KD spans output-level (soft-target) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and protocol variants such as offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data-free, and privacy-aware workflows. In practice KD is frequently combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and must be tailored to teacher/student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; while empirical results across modalities often show students can recover much of teacher performance, important challenges remain in handling capacity mismatch, data scarcity, bias and robustness, and formal theoretical guarantees.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated family of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD encompasses logit/soft-target transfer, intermediate-feature and relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation, online and data-free variants, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Its practical strengths include enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, improving generalization and some robustness properties, and serving as a core component of compression pipelines when used with task-aware design choices. At the same time, KD exhibits clear failure modes—teacher–student mismatch, bias transfer, poor preservation of low-frequency behaviors, and sensitivity to data availability and domain shift—that motivate complementary methods and targeted research into robust, privacy-preserving, and automated distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Colon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger or ensembled teacher models to compact students. Across vision and natural language processing, KD methods include matching teacher logits, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data‑free or privacy‑aware variants. Empirical evidence shows KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss and—when combined with architectural or training strategies—can sometimes match or exceed teacher performance. However, KD is context dependent: outcomes hinge on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection, the particular signals transferred, and complementary compression steps such as pruning or quantization. Open challenges include propagating teacher errors and biases, preserving rare or structured behaviors, working under scarce or private data, and robustness to distribution shift. The most reliable deployments treat KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone cure.

papers_seen.author: Merritt
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central and practical family of techniques for transferring information from larger, often ensemble or overparameterized teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. KD methods operate at multiple granularities (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals, attention maps, and adversarial or generator-based surrogate data) and are widely used across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs, and multimodal tasks). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can substantially reduce model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, the availability and selection of data (including synthesized or public data in privacy-sensitive settings), and how KD is combined with complementary compression methods. Key open problems include handling teacher–student mismatch, preserving low-frequency or minority phenomena, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and automating teacher and objective design for optimal transfer.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single trick into a broad, practical family of methods for compressing large models into smaller, faster, or privacy-aware models while retaining much of their performance. The techniques differ by what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel statistics), how the transfer is staged (offline teacher-student, online/co-distillation, data-free/zero-shot, few-shot), and which complementary strategies are used (projectors, mixup/data augmentation, pruning, or architecture-aware design). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as information transfer and as a regularizer; success depends critically on choices about teacher signals, student capacity, the availability and nature of data, and task-specific design. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation under limited or private data, preventing transfer of teacher errors, adapting to heterogeneous or federated settings, and scaling distillation to very large models and complex structured-output tasks.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. A broad toolkit has emerged — soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational/contrastive objectives, multi- and self-distillation, data-free or synthetic-data schemes, and hybrid pipelines combining distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirically, KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and objective design. Important open problems include principled theory linking transfer signals to student generalization, reliable distillation under domain shift and heterogeneous devices, and preserving rare or structured outputs in sequence tasks.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Practical, but Insufficiently Complete Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has proven to be a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks. It supports multiple transfer targets (logits, features, attention, relational signals), multi-teacher and data-free setups, and integrates naturally with complementary compression methods. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and task-aware objective design. To realize KD’s full potential in real-world deployments, practitioners must treat it as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context-Dependent Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their predictive performance. KD operates at multiple levels—from soft-target (logit) supervision to representation- and layer-wise alignment—and integrates naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-augmentation or curriculum strategies. Empirical evidence across vision, language, generative models, and retrieval shows distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher accuracy and can add benefits such as improved generalization or interpretability when applied carefully. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, optimization choices, and explicit handling of teacher biases and distribution shift. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component in a broader compression pipeline, chosen and tuned to the task, data availability, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Knight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task‑Aware Component of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical paradigm for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. When treated as a configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline and combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data strategies, or privacy-preserving protocols), KD routinely yields strong empirical gains across vision, language, multimodal, and federated settings. However, KD is not a one‑size‑fits‑all remedy: its success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student alignment, the choice of distillation signals, data availability or synthesis, and explicit measures to mitigate propagated errors, distribution shift, and fairness or privacy concerns. I argue KD should be used as a task‑aware toolbox—selected and tuned to task, data, and deployment constraints—rather than as a single fixed recipe.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Synthesis of the Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible, empirically validated family of techniques for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller students. Across modalities and training protocols, distillation operates at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware design. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and alignment, data availability or synthesis, and careful objective and optimization design; important limitations include teacher error propagation, impaired modeling of low-frequency phenomena, and distribution-shift vulnerabilities.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, or more deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. The literature develops multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), training protocols (offline multi-stage, online, self-distillation, data-free/generative, adversarial), and application-specific adaptations (NLP transformer compression, vision, speech, graph models, federated and privacy-aware settings). Empirical work shows KD frequently yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when paired with architecture-aware design and complementary compression methods, while remaining sensitive to teacher quality, data availability, and distributional or fairness concerns. Practical success generally requires matching the distillation objective to the task, handling data limitations with augmentation or synthetic generators, and integrating KD into a broader compression portfolio (pruning, quantization, architecture search).

papers_seen.author: Ferguson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their performance. KD has been extended from soft-label/logit transfer to a rich set of representation- and task-level objectives (feature matching, attention and relation alignment, projector modules, online/multi-teacher schemes, and data-free methods). When applied with task awareness — choosing what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data, privacy, and hardware constraints — KD consistently enables substantial reductions in size and latency with modest accuracy loss. However, KD is not a panacea: its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and alignment, data availability, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases and low-frequency behaviors. Best practice treats KD as a configurable element of an integrated compression pipeline combined with pruning, quantization, and hardware-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Path for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from teacher models. Across tasks and modalities, distillation methods—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature and structure-preserving objectives—enable deployable models that retain much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory use, and communication cost. Distillation also serves as a flexible substrate for addressing domain adaptation, lifelong learning, robustness, low-precision deployment, and generator compression. However, realizing these benefits in practice requires careful design choices around what to transfer, how to map layers and representations, how to handle limited or private teacher data, and how to mitigate bias or robustness loss.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger or specialized teacher models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. Across modalities and tasks, researchers have developed many variants—logit transfer, feature- and attention-level matching, relational and contrastive objectives, ensemble- and teacher-aware algorithms, data-free and few-shot protocols, and meta-learned teachers—to address practical deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, device heterogeneity) while also pursuing robustness, fairness, and task adaptation. This synthesis summarizes dominant methods, representative applications, empirical patterns, and common failure modes that guide practical use and future research.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Practical, but Conditional — Toward Task‑Aware, Integrated Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information at many levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and supports a wide range of protocols (offline teacher→student, online co‑distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free or privacy‑aware schemes). Empirical evidence shows KD frequently preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute, but its success depends on task awareness, teacher–student alignment, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases. Best practice therefore treats KD as the configurable core of a broader compression pipeline that combines appropriate distillation objectives with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, data strategies) tailored to the target task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Thomas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, Applications, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applied approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, retrieval, and generative settings, KD variants—matching soft logits, aligning intermediate features or attention, relational and contrastive objectives, and data- or privacy-aware synthesis—enable substantial efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance when designed with task-aware objectives and appropriate data strategies. Practical deployment treats KD as a configurable core within integrated compression pipelines that also leverage pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data augmentation; remaining challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity and privacy constraints, low-frequency/long-tail phenomena, and principled layer alignment across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Durham
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated family of methods for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants—from soft-logit supervision to intermediate-feature and relational/contrastive objectives, online and multi-teacher schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols—enable reduced memory, latency, and communication costs while often preserving most teacher performance. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and task- or data-aware procedures; its reliable application requires explicit attention to teacher–student compatibility, data availability, optimization schedules, and safeguards for bias, rare-case behavior, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Configurable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable paradigm for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when its objectives, data strategies, and student architectures are chosen with task and deployment constraints in mind. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful mitigation of transferred biases and robustness gaps. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core within an integrated compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data- or privacy-aware synthesis.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Benefits, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring predictive and representational information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy. KD has been adapted to diverse transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational maps), multi-teacher schemes, data-free or few-shot regimes, and domain- or task-adaptive pipelines. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful teacher–student design, KD routinely yields large reductions in model size and runtime while preserving most of the teacher's performance. However, distillation is not automatic: practitioner attention is needed to address teacher selection, data availability and distribution shift, capacity mismatch, low-frequency behavior, and risk of transferring biases or teacher artifacts.
