papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Sims
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Insights, and Applications (Synthesis)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. A broad toolkit has emerged — including logits/soft-label transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, adversarial and contrastive objectives, online and self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search — enabling deployment across vision, speech, language, generative, and multimodal settings. Empirical and theoretical work highlights gains in latency, memory, calibration, and sometimes robustness, while pointing to failure modes driven by teacher quality, capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and distribution shift; best practice treats KD as a core element of a broader, context-aware compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with task‑aware distillation objectives, appropriate data strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD routinely delivers strong efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks. However, realizing robust, fair, and reliable compressed models requires careful attention to teacher–student alignment, the nature and availability of distillation data, and targeted remedies for known failure modes such as bias transfer, degradation on low‑frequency phenomena, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad toolkit—ranging from soft logits to intermediate-feature and adversarial or data-free methods—has been developed and applied across vision, language, speech, and multimodal problems. Practical success depends on matching the distilled signal to student capacity and data regime, combining KD with other compression methods, and explicitly addressing known failure modes such as teacher bias, capacity mismatch, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Castaneda
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Toolbox for Model Compression: Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or specialized students. Empirical and theoretical work across vision, language, graph, and generative domains shows KD can substantially reduce inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but its success depends on choices about transfer targets, data availability, teacher quality, and complementary compression methods. Treating KD as a principled toolbox—combining logits, feature- and relation-level objectives, data strategies, and hardware-aware techniques—yields the most reliable route to practical, robust compression.

papers_seen.author: Curtis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse toolkit of distillation objectives and training protocols has been developed, and KD is most effective when treated as a configurable element within an integrated compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware design and complementary primitives (e.g., pruning, quantization). Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the availability and selection of distillation data (or reliable synthesis strategies), and careful protocol design to mitigate robustness, fairness, and privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Configurable Core of Model Compression: Evidence, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an empirically validated, flexible family of methods for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger teachers into smaller students. KD routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs when the distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, and data strategies are chosen to match the task and deployment constraints. However, KD is not an automatic solution: it requires representation-aware objectives, careful handling of data and capacity mismatch, and integration with complementary compression primitives and safeguards to avoid failure modes such as bias transfer, loss of rare behaviors, and domain-shift fragility. When treated as a configurable core component of a compression pipeline rather than a plug-and-play fix, KD enables responsible, practical deployment of deep models across vision, language, multimodal, and industrial systems.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers across vision, language, graph, recommendation, and generative settings. KD encompasses a range of techniques—soft-target matching, intermediate feature and attention alignment, contrastive and adversarial objectives, layer- and channel-wise mappings, and data- or task-aware variants—and is frequently combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can enable deployable, lower-latency models, improve robustness and interpretability in some settings, and serve as a substrate for domain adaptation and privacy-aware workflows; its success depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, data availability (including data-free or few-shot regimes), and practical engineering choices.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, evidence-backed approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable models across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. KD methods — ranging from logits transfer to intermediate-feature matching, self-distillation, and selective-sample protocols — routinely enable substantial reductions in compute, memory, and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not automatic: success depends on what information is transferred, teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data choices, and integration with complementary compression techniques. When treated as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline, KD provides a practical route to deploy high-performing models under resource, privacy, and latency constraints.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Practical Model Compression: Evidence, Techniques, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable paradigm for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the performance of larger networks. Across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs, and generative models) and use-cases (edge deployment, federated learning, domain adaptation, continual learning), distillation has repeatedly enabled dramatic reductions in model size and inference cost while maintaining or even improving task performance. However, distillation is not a panacea: careful design of what to transfer (logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure), how to align teacher and student inputs and layers, and when to apply supplementary strategies (adversarial examples, multi-teacher weighting, continual updates) is necessary to avoid failure modes such as propagated teacher errors, misalignment across detectors, and limits in compressing some model families. Drawing on empirical results and method innovations across the literature, I argue that KD should be treated as a foundational component of any deployment-oriented model compression pipeline, and that combining complementary distillation techniques tailored to the task and architecture yields the best balance of compactness, speed, and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically motivated family of techniques for transferring behavior from larger or ensemble teacher models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. KD methods operate at multiple levels of abstraction (output logits, intermediate features, attention and relational maps), can be adapted to scarce- or privacy-constrained data regimes, and are commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet deployment constraints. Empirically, KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance across vision and language tasks, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of transfer targets, and the availability or synthesis of appropriate distillation data. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a turnkey solution.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically supported set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD operates at multiple levels—soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational structures—and is effective across modalities (vision, language, speech, and translation) when adapted to task constraints. KD achieves substantial reductions in latency and model size while preserving much of teacher performance, but it is not a turnkey solution: its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit measures to mitigate transferred biases and low-frequency or out-of-distribution failures. Consequently, KD should be treated as a configurable, central component of an integrated compression and deployment pipeline rather than as a standalone recipe.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller student models. KD routinely yields large efficiency gains (reduced memory, compute, and latency) while preserving much of teacher performance when applied with task‑aware objectives, appropriate teacher–student alignment, and complementary compression methods. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on what signals are transferred, teacher quality, student capacity, data availability (including privacy or data‑free regimes), and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer and degraded handling of rare phenomena. Treated as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline and combined with targeted algorithmic and engineering practices, KD enables practical, deployable compression across modalities and settings.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques reduce model size and inference cost by transferring information from larger, more expensive models (teachers) to smaller, cheaper models (students). Across modalities and tasks, researchers have developed logit- and feature-level distillation, layer-wise and many-to-many layer matching, task-aware filtering, projector-based adapters, meta-learned teachers, multi-teacher weighting, and data- or privacy-constrained workflows. Empirical work demonstrates that carefully designed distillation protocols can retain much of teacher performance (and sometimes improve generalization) while enabling deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy; theoretical analyses offer insight into when soft labels help and when hard labels are necessary. Remaining challenges include bridging capacity gaps, dealing with mismatched architectures and modalities, operating without original data, and guaranteeing privacy under compression.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Flexible, but Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective and adaptable framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. KD supports many transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational structure) and training paradigms (offline, online, multi‑teacher, data‑free), enabling substantial reductions in inference cost when integrated with complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, available data (or the ability to synthesize it), and deliberate mitigation of failure modes such as transferred bias, distribution shift, and degraded performance on rare outputs. I argue that KD should be treated as a central, configurable component of compression pipelines—powerful when designed and combined with other methods, but requiring task‑aware engineering and explicit safeguards to be reliable in practice.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Frost

Empirical work shows that careful choice of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data and low-frequency phenomena materially affects student quality and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Practical, and Careful Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP

However, reliable application requires attention to teacher quality, layer mapping, sample selection, and interactions with regularization and pretraining; when designed for the target task and environment, KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance and unlock real-world deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: This synthesis summarizes what the provided literature collectively reports about knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques: commonly used distillation objectives and training protocols, empirical patterns of when and how KD helps across modalities, practical constraints and failure modes (data availability, teacher–student mismatch, low-frequency/structured outputs, privacy and bias transfer), and targeted solutions (data-free/zero-shot distillation, teacher engineering, multi-teacher and curriculum schemes, and combinations with pruning/quantization and architecture search). The goal is to give a concise map of methods, observed trade-offs, and open problems for researchers and practitioners working on compressing or adapting large models for resource- or deployment-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Wolf

KD is best treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, augmentation, or synthetic-data strategies—rather than as a standalone panacea.

papers_seen.author: Zimmerman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Benefits, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a versatile, multi-faceted toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. KD variants transfer information via soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure, contrastive or adversarial objectives, and can operate in offline, online, self-distillation, or data‑free regimes. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most of a teacher’s accuracy while producing meaningful reductions in parameters, latency, memory, and communication cost. However, KD is not automatic: its success depends on matching distilled signals to the task and student capacity, selecting or synthesizing appropriate data, and combining distillation with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical pipelines treat KD as a configurable component within a broader compression and deployment strategy that explicitly addresses teacher imperfection, distribution shift, rare behaviors, privacy, and architecture heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Pollard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for training smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teacher models. Across vision, language, graphs, and multimodal tasks, KD methods transfer predictive and representational signals (soft logits, internal features, attention maps, relational or contrastive signals) and operate under a range of training protocols (offline teacher→student, online/co-distillation, multi-teacher, self-distillation, and data-free or synthetic-data approaches). Empirical work shows KD often recovers much of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, distillation signals, and data strategy are chosen carefully. Practical deployment typically treats KD as a core, configurable component of a broader compression pipeline that also includes pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data-side strategies. Open challenges include principled theory of transferable signals, robust distillation under data scarcity and heterogeneity, privacy-aware or data-free methods, and preserving low-frequency or long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from teacher to student. A broad family of distillation techniques has been developed—logit (soft-label) matching, feature and layer-wise mimicry, multi-teacher and confidence-weighted schemes, adversarial and contrastive objectives, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants—enabling deployment across vision, language, graphs, recommender systems, and federated settings. While distillation often preserves most teacher performance and can even improve student generalization, effectiveness depends on what is transferred, layer alignment, teacher quality, availability and match of data, and complementary compression methods. This synthesis summarizes the operational variants, key empirical findings, domain-specific applications, common failure modes, and practical recommendations distilled from the provided studies.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied framework for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teacher models into compact student models. A wide range of distillation objectives (logit/soft-target matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational and contrastive losses), training protocols (offline, online/self-, multi-teacher), and data strategies (full-data, limited-data, data-free, and privacy-aware synthesis) have been proposed and combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical studies show KD often recovers much of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, and suitable data strategies are available, but KD is context-dependent and must be integrated with task-aware design choices to manage limits related to teacher–student mismatch, optimization, data scarcity, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient students so they can be deployed under latency, memory, privacy, and device-heterogeneity constraints. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods—ranging from soft-label matching to intermediate-feature, attention, and relational alignment—are combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data or systems strategies (multi-teacher supervision, synthetic-data generation, federated protocols) to produce favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. The practical effectiveness of KD depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, data availability, and mitigation of bias or robustness issues.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably transfers behavior from large teacher models into smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in latency, memory and compute while preserving much of task performance. KD techniques span logits/soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level alignment, relational and contrastive signals, online and multi-teacher protocols, and data-free or domain-adaptive variants. Empirical evidence shows KD is a practical first-line strategy for deployment across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, but it is not a standalone cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, objective design, and careful integration with complementary compression tools. For robust, real-world deployment, KD should be treated as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline combined with targeted engineering to mitigate failure modes such as capacity mismatch, data scarcity, bias propagation, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster, or deployment‑specialized student models. Across vision, language, speech, multimodal, and federated settings, KD methods—including soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial or data‑free generation, and self- or online‑distillation—enable substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while often preserving a large fraction of teacher performance. Practical success depends on aligning distillation signals to student capacity and task requirements, selecting or synthesizing suitable data, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Important limitations remain (teacher–student capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, failures on low‑frequency phenomena, and distribution shift), so KD is best used as a configurable component within an integrated, task‑aware compression pipeline with explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. A broad toolkit has emerged — soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational/contrastive objectives, multi- and self-distillation, data-free or synthetic-data schemes, and hybrid pipelines combining distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirically, KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and objective design. Important open problems include principled theory linking transfer signals to student generalization, reliable distillation under domain shift and heterogeneous devices, and preserving rare or structured outputs in sequence tasks.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practically essential approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster, or specialized models. When designed around task constraints, student capacity, and available data, KD preserves much of a teacher's capabilities while enabling deployment under compute, memory, latency, and privacy limits. Its greatest value comes from treating distillation as a configurable toolkit—combining soft-targets, representation matching, adversarial or data-free sample synthesis, and multi-teacher or self-distillation—with complementary compression techniques to meet real-world constraints. Success requires careful handling of teacher–student alignment, data scarcity, distribution shift, and bias transfer, but a task-aware, hybrid pipeline makes KD one of the most practical routes to effective model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad, practical toolkit for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger networks. Across vision, language, graphs, speech, and generative modeling, researchers transfer information via softened output distributions, intermediate-feature matching, relational and attention maps, and many-to-many layer alignment. Variants address resource heterogeneity, data unavailability, privacy, robustness, and fairness. Empirical and analytic work shows that distillation combines information transfer with regularization effects, but its success depends on design choices (what to transfer, teacher quality, data or pseudo-data, and alignment losses). State-of-the-art practice mixes logits-based loss with feature- or representation-level objectives, task-aware augmentations, and architecture- or training-aware modifications to obtain favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs in deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context‑Aware Component of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful and versatile family of techniques for producing compact student models from larger teachers, but its effectiveness is strongly context dependent. For reliable, high‑fidelity compression in deep learning and NLP, distillation should be treated as a core element of an integrated, task‑aware compression pipeline that combines careful teacher–student design, appropriate distilled signals, data strategies (including data‑free or privacy‑sensitive variants), and complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques form a diverse set of methods for producing smaller, faster, or more deployable models by transferring knowledge from larger or specialized models. Approaches span from simple soft-label supervision to richer transfers of internal representations, intermediate-layer mappings, attention-guided projections, adversarial feature alignment, and task- or device-aware compression. KD is used across domains—image classification, detection (2D and 3D), recommendation/CTR, language model compression, federated and heterogeneous-device learning, and reinforcement learning—and is frequently combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or curriculum strategies. Recent work examines theoretical aspects (e.g., bias–variance tradeoffs and statistical interactions with data augmentation), practical design choices (teacher-student layer alignment, many-to-many mappings, ensemble teachers), and extensions that address privacy, fairness, and low-data regimes. Despite strong empirical success, open problems remain in understanding when particular KD variants best transfer generalization, how to measure and mitigate transferred biases, and how to optimally combine KD with other compression primitives for different constraints.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for producing smaller, faster, and often more deployable models from larger teachers. Across vision, language, multimodal systems, and specialized domains such as healthcare and novel-view synthesis, KD yields large reductions in parameter count and inference cost while retaining most of the teacher performance when applied with task-aware design choices. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on what information is transferred (logits, features, relational structure), the availability and nature of data, teacher quality and design, and careful integration with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Pragmatic deployment requires attention to robustness, bias propagation, data scarcity, and domain mismatch, and benefits most from combining KD with task- and hardware-aware practices.

papers_seen.author: Curry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses information from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Research and practice have developed a diverse toolkit — matching soft logits, imitating intermediate features and attention, using contrastive/relational objectives, generating or selecting distillation data, multi-teacher and online schemes, and combining KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work across vision, language, recommendation, speech, and multimodal tasks shows distilled students frequently recover much of teacher performance, though effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and alignment of objectives and representations. Key open problems include reliable transfer of rare or structured behaviors, robust distillation under data heterogeneity and privacy constraints, principled teacher selection and co-design, and automated, task-aware distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical tool for compressing large models into efficient students, but it must be applied conditionally and integrated with task‑aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques. KD delivers strong empirical gains across modalities when teacher quality, student capacity, distilled signals, and data regimes are aligned; however, known failure modes (teacher–student mismatch, limited or absent data, propagation of teacher artifacts, and degradation on low‑frequency phenomena) require targeted remedies and validation for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable framework for producing compact models from larger teachers. When designed and deployed with attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and complementary compression primitives, KD routinely yields substantial gains in efficiency with limited loss in task performance. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on task- and deployment‑aware choices, and important open problems remain in robustness, fairness, data‑free and privacy‑constrained settings, and principled theory linking distilled signals to student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses and transfers predictive ability from large, expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student models. Across modalities and architectures, KD variants extend beyond matching teacher output probabilities to include internal representation matching, contrastive objectives, adversarial learning, selective sample supervision, and data- or privacy-aware protocols. These methods enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, reduce inference latency, support domain adaptation and federated settings, and in some cases improve student generalization beyond the teacher. Practical challenges include input/representation mismatches between teacher and student, propagation of teacher biases (e.g., low-frequency lexical errors), and the need for careful selection of what is distilled and how. Empirically, tailored distillation objectives and training procedures—such as internal-representation matching, progressive module replacement, ensemble distillation, and contrastive or relational objectives—have produced strong compression results across vision, language, graph-structured data, and generative scene models.

papers_seen.author: Guerrero
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD supports many transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational constraints), can be adapted to data‑limited and data‑free regimes, and combines productively with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). However, reliable deployment requires task‑aware design: selecting appropriate distillation objectives, aligning teacher and student capacities and architectures, addressing data regimes and privacy constraints, and mitigating failure modes such as bias transfer and degradation on rare or low‑frequency phenomena. Treated as a configurable core of compression pipelines and paired with targeted algorithmic and engineering practices, KD enables practical, deployable model compression across modalities and settings.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. KD techniques encompass output-level supervision (soft logits), representation- and attention-level matching, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free synthesis, progressive module replacement, and online or multi-teacher protocols. Empirical evidence shows KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost, but success is context-sensitive: it depends on teacher quality and design, student capacity and architecture alignment, the availability and distribution of data (including data-free or synthesized alternatives), and careful loss and layer-mapping choices. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a configurable toolbox to be combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and domain-, fairness-, or privacy-aware interventions. Remaining scientific and engineering challenges include principled selection of distillation targets, reliable distillation under limited or mismatched data, mitigation of transferred biases and rare-token degradation, theoretical understanding of when and why different KD objectives help, and automated, hardware-aware co-design for heterogeneous deployment.

papers_seen.author: Durham
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated family of methods for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants—from soft-logit supervision to intermediate-feature and relational/contrastive objectives, online and multi-teacher schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols—enable reduced memory, latency, and communication costs while often preserving most teacher performance. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and task- or data-aware procedures; its reliable application requires explicit attention to teacher–student compatibility, data availability, optimization schedules, and safeguards for bias, rare-case behavior, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of methods for transferring information from larger or more expensive models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models. Methods span from classic logit-based distillation to feature- and representation-level matching, adversarial and projector-based strategies, module-replacement and pruning approaches, and specialized protocols for cross-modal, federated, data-free, and generative settings. Applications range across NLP (BERT compression, machine translation, non-autoregressive models), speech and paralinguistic embeddings, vision (image translation, novel-view synthesis), 3D detection, recommender systems, and graph neural networks. Research highlights include analyses that explain why distillation works, techniques that mitigate transfer of teacher errors, curricula and selection mechanisms for better sample usage, and approaches that adapt distillation to privacy- or resource-constrained environments. Together, these works map an ecosystem of practical techniques and open challenges for deploying compact, high-performing models in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Carter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for producing compact, efficient models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. KD encompasses approaches that match teacher outputs (soft logits), intermediate features or attention, relational and contrastive signals, and methods that operate with or without access to original training data. When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and matched to task- and data-specific constraints, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in parameters and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. However, effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, choice of distilled signals, data availability and preparation, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Important open problems remain in principled selection of distillation targets, reliable distillation under limited or private data, mitigation of bias transfer, and theory connecting distilled signals to student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Practical Necessity, Limitations, and a Consolidated Best-Practice Agenda
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques are now essential for deploying high‑performing deep models in resource‑constrained settings across vision, speech, recommendation, graph, and language tasks. KD delivers large efficiency gains while often preserving much of teacher performance, but it is not a turnkey solution: teacher inference cost, data mismatches introduced by distillation, low‑frequency token degradation, privacy considerations, and heterogeneous deployment constraints each demand tailored remedies. Combining complementary strategies — multi‑teacher distillation, student‑aware teacher design, projector/feature adaptation, self‑distillation, exposure to raw data, and privacy-aware or federated KD — yields robust compressed models that approach or match teacher capabilities in practice.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Bradshaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted family of techniques for transferring behavior and representations from larger or composite teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD spans soft-target/logit matching, intermediate feature and attention imitation, relational or contrastive objectives, self- and multi-teacher schemes, and data-free or generator-based approaches; it is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and pretraining to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work across vision, speech, graphs, and natural language processing shows KD can substantially reduce model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance, but its practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and careful choice of transfer targets and training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: The Efficacy and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into efficient students across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models, and reinforcement learning). Empirical work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance while offering substantial inference speedups and parameter reductions, and can be enhanced by targeted techniques (data augmentation, intermediate-layer matching, multi-teacher schedules, contrastive objectives, and meta-learning). However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends strongly on distillation procedure, data complexity, teacher–student alignment, and training dynamics. Practical deployment requires selecting distillation objectives and data strategies that address robustness, limited-data regimes, privacy/federation, and modality-specific needs.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical strategy for compressing large models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable students across modalities and tasks. KD techniques extend beyond matching logits: they include internal-representation distillation, adversarial and relational approaches, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware methods, and architecture-aware replacements. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can preserve or even improve generalization, enable domain adaptation, and permit deployment under resource, privacy, or latency constraints—provided practitioners attend to known failure modes such as teacher bias, low-frequency lexical errors, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or specialized models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. A broad toolkit has emerged — matching soft logits, imitating intermediate features and attention, relational and contrastive objectives, ensemble and multi-teacher schemes, adversarial or data-free sample synthesis, and layer-mapping strategies — and these methods are combined routinely with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Distillation is effective across modalities (vision, language, multimodal) and tasks (classification, generation, detection, retrieval, ranking), but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, availability and nature of distillation data, and task-specific design choices. Practical deployments therefore emphasize task-aware selection of distilled signals, pretraining of compact models, and targeted mitigation of failure modes such as transferred biases and degradation on low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal domains, a diverse set of distillation targets (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure) and training protocols (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, multi‑teacher, data‑free or self‑distillation) have been developed. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often recover much of a teacher’s performance while enabling lower latency, reduced memory use, and new deployment modes; success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful design of the transfer objective. Practical pipelines commonly pair KD with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task‑aware procedures (layer mapping, curriculum, teacher adaptation) to meet deployment constraints. Important open problems include robust transfer under distribution shift and data scarcity, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, principled automated design for heterogeneous student architectures, and privacy‑aware or data‑free distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of methods for transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models so that students achieve improved accuracy, latency, or resource use while retaining much of teacher behavior. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, internal features, relational structure, or contrastive/global representations), how supervision is scheduled (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation), and how distillation is combined with other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows substantial gains across vision, language, graphs, recommendation, and generative models, but limitations remain around data availability, teacher-student mismatch, low-frequency information transfer, privacy constraints, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of methods for transferring information from large, expensive models (or ensembles) to smaller, efficient models. Methods include logit-based distillation, feature- or representation-based matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher strategies, data-free and privacy-preserving approaches, and combinations with pruning or architecture search. KD has been applied across modalities and domains—vision, language, graphs, reinforcement learning, generative models, and healthcare—demonstrating gains in inference efficiency, robustness, generalization, and interpretability when appropriately designed. Open challenges remain around data availability, teacher–student mismatch, selection of distilled signals and samples, and principled integration with other compression techniques; recent work proposes meta-learning teachers, adaptive teacher weighting, projector modules, and task-adaptive compression as practical remedies.
