papers_seen.author: Sanders
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central, Conditional, and Best-Practice‑Driven for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central and practical approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers across vision, language, speech, and multimodal settings. KD provides a flexible family of mechanisms (soft-targets, feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data-free or federated protocols) that, when combined with complementary compression primitives and task-aware design, yield strong empirical trade-offs between efficiency and performance. However, KD is not universally sufficient: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of transferred biases. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component within an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone recipe.

papers_seen.author: Rasmussen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Practical Necessity, Limits, and a Best-Practice Agenda
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large models into smaller, faster students for deployment across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks. Empirical work shows distillation can recover much of a teacher's performance while enabling reduced memory, lower-latency inference, and new capabilities such as task-adaptive compression, multi-task transfer, and interpretable surrogates. At the same time, distillation is not a turnkey remedy: optimization challenges, dataset and distribution mismatches, teacher bias transfer, and design choices about what to transfer (logits, features, relational structure) strongly affect outcomes. The most reliable results come from combining KD with complementary techniques (teacher adaptation, selective or curriculum-driven sample selection, representation matching, low-precision numerics, and scaled training procedures) and from tailoring the procedure to task- and deployment-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable method for transferring functionality from large teacher models to smaller students so that compressed models retain much of the teacher's performance while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and communication. KD covers a spectrum of techniques—from soft-target matching to internal representation transfer, multi-teacher/online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware approaches, and architecture-aware solutions such as task-adaptive compression—and integrates naturally with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, adversarial training). When implemented with care about teacher selection, data selection or synthesis, and representation alignment, KD enables practical deployment of high-performing models across modalities; when misapplied it can propagate teacher errors, amplify biases, or fail due to optimization and data-mismatch issues. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a first-order engineering primitive for model compression in deep learning and NLP, and outlines recommended practices and known limitations to guide responsible adoption.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical paradigm for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, multimodal and generative settings. KD techniques transfer teacher behavior via soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational objectives, and can be extended to data-free, privacy-preserving, and adversarial regimes. Best results arise when distillation is combined with task-aware design choices and complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search); remaining challenges include data- or domain-limited scenarios, teacher–student mismatch, robustness and privacy trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Lane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient Tool — Integrating Distillation into Robust Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically effective approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency across vision and NLP. However, KD alone rarely solves all deployment challenges: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, and objective design. The most reliable practice treats KD as a configurable core component embedded within integrated compression pipelines that combine representation alignment, data or data‑free strategies, and architecture- and hardware-aware methods.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible set of methods for transferring knowledge from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models to enable deployment under constraints of compute, memory, latency, or privacy. Across vision and natural language tasks, distillation targets range from soft logits to intermediate representations and relational signals; KD is frequently combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with domain- or task-specific procedures to improve efficacy. KD delivers strong empirical gains in many settings but is bounded by teacher quality, availability and match of data, teacher–student capacity gaps, and the risk of transferring teacher biases; effective application therefore requires task-aware choices of signals, data strategies, and often hybrid compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Curry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses information from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. Research and practice have developed a diverse toolkit — matching soft logits, imitating intermediate features and attention, using contrastive/relational objectives, generating or selecting distillation data, multi-teacher and online schemes, and combining KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work across vision, language, recommendation, speech, and multimodal tasks shows distilled students frequently recover much of teacher performance, though effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and alignment of objectives and representations. Key open problems include reliable transfer of rare or structured behaviors, robust distillation under data heterogeneity and privacy constraints, principled teacher selection and co-design, and automated, task-aware distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: The Centrality of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are indispensable for moving state-of-the-art deep models from research to real-world deployment. By transferring predictive behavior, representations, or relational structure from larger or specialized teachers to smaller students, KD enables faster inference, smaller footprints, better generalization across domains, privacy-preserving sharing, and adaptation to heterogeneous hardware and data constraints. Realizing these benefits in practice requires combining algorithmic advances (multi-teacher regimes, curriculum and projector design, augmentation and adversarial synthesis), systems thinking (federated and client-inclusive protocols), and attention to pitfalls (mismatched objectives, erased class relations). Together, the literature shows KD is not a niche trick but a broad, flexible toolkit for addressing latency, capacity, distribution shift, privacy, and interpretability in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, more efficient student models. Across vision, language, speech, and other modalities KD routinely yields favorable efficiency–accuracy trade-offs when it is treated as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline. Practical success requires choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to manage or synthesize distillation data, and how to combine KD with complementary compression methods. Important open problems include reliably preserving robustness and long‑tail behaviors, principled teacher–student co‑design, and safe use under privacy and fairness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large or ensemble teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD variants—ranging from soft-logit matching to layer- and feature-level alignment, attention transfer, adversarial/contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free synthesis—regularly enable substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Practical success requires matching distillation objectives to task and student capacity, choosing appropriate data strategies, and integrating KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Important open issues include optimization and capacity gaps, teacher-bias transfer, limited- or no-data scenarios, domain shift, privacy guarantees, and automated teacher–student co-design.

papers_seen.author: Manning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Practical, but Insufficient — A Position and Recommended Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely adopted framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. Empirical evidence across vision and language shows that KD can reduce inference cost, latency, and memory requirements and enable deployment under privacy, communication, and resource constraints. However, KD alone does not guarantee robust, unbiased, or optimal compressed models: failures arise from teacher–student mismatch, limited or absent data, transfer of teacher errors and biases, poor handling of low-frequency phenomena, and vulnerability under distribution shift or adversarial attack. Practical compression therefore treats KD as a core component within an integrated pipeline—combining representation-aware objectives, curriculum and sample-selection strategies, adversarial or synthetic-data generation for data-scarce regimes, and complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to realize reliable, resource-aware students.

papers_seen.author: Hopkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller students. Across modalities and tasks KD methods—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to feature- and relation-level imitation, contrastive and adversarial schemes, and data‑free generation—regularly produce large size and latency reductions with modest performance loss when designed in a task- and deployment-aware way. Practical success is conditional on teacher quality, data regime, teacher–student alignment, and safeguards against propagation of undesirable teacher properties; addressing open problems (robust data-free distillation, theory of transfer, fairness and privacy) requires integrating KD into end-to-end compression pipelines and co-designing students, objectives, and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Vang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Findings, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller student models. KD encompasses a range of transfer targets and training protocols and is commonly combined with complementary compression methods to meet deployment constraints. Practical success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis strategies, and careful choice of distilled signals and training procedures.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad family of KD objectives and workflows—soft-target matching, intermediate-representation mimicking, relational or attention-map transfer, multi-teacher and self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants—has been developed and applied across vision, language, graph, and recommendation settings. Empirical and theoretical work demonstrates substantial practical gains in latency, memory, and deployability when KD is combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware mapping), but success depends on careful choices about teacher quality, student capacity, data, and objective design; remaining challenges include optimization difficulties, distribution shift, rare-token performance, and bias or privacy leakage.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. A broad family of distillation targets and training protocols has been developed and applied across vision, language, generative, and multimodal tasks; KD typically recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when matched to student capacity and data conditions. Practical deployments treat KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies—rather than as a standalone cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques are widely used to produce smaller, faster models while preserving much of the performance of large teachers. Approaches vary from matching final logits to transferring internal representations, attention maps, or layer-wise information, and they are applied across modalities including NLP, vision, speech, and reinforcement learning. Practical extensions address multi-teacher setups, data-free scenarios, domain adaptation, quantization, and architecture-aware compression; remaining challenges include handling heterogeneous architectures, data heterogeneity, fairness, and reliably preserving inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teachers' performance. Across modalities and tasks—classification, generation, retrieval, structured prediction, and language tasks—KD variants (logit transfer, feature- and attention-matching, adversarial and contrastive objectives, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols) provide concrete trade-offs between model size, compute, and accuracy. When combined with complementary strategies such as architecture search, pruning, low-precision numerics, or privacy mechanisms, distillation enables robust deployment on resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive platforms. However, distillation outcomes depend on teacher quality, data availability, teacher–student alignment, and design choices for objectives and training pipelines; tailored practices are therefore needed to realize KD's full potential and avoid failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a practical, flexible approach to compressing large neural models into resource-efficient students while preserving much of the teachers' performance. Across modalities and tasks — from language and retrieval to vision, generation, and graph learning — distillation techniques enable trade-offs between accuracy, compute, and memory that make deployment feasible on constrained hardware. However, the effectiveness of distillation depends strongly on the distillation objective, the information transferred (probabilities, internal representations, or structured signals), availability of original data, and care to avoid transferring undesirable teacher properties. When combined with complementary compression techniques (quantization, architecture search, low-precision training, or curriculum strategies), distillation can yield compact models that approach or sometimes even exceed teacher performance while meeting practical latency and size constraints.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Best Practices and Limitations of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a broadly applicable and powerful approach for compressing models across modalities, but its effectiveness depends on design choices spanning what is distilled (logits, features, internal representations), how inputs are prepared (augmentation, sample selection), how multiple teachers are reconciled, and whether robustness or task-specific structure is considered. Recent work shows that combining soft-target regularization with feature- and intermediate-representation matching, careful input-side interventions, and adaptive distillation objectives yields the best tradeoffs between compression, accuracy, and robustness across vision, language, multimodal, graph, and generative-model settings.

papers_seen.author: Rivas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a rich, task-sensitive toolbox for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models to compact students. Practitioners move beyond simple logit matching to transfer internal representations, attention patterns, relational structure, and decision-boundary information, and they combine distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation). Empirical results across vision, language, generative models, and structured prediction show distilled students often recover much of teacher performance and can enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but distillation also has failure modes—teacher bias transfer, sensitivity to data availability, capacity mismatch, and degraded modeling of low-frequency phenomena—that require targeted mitigations and continued theoretical and empirical work.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large models into smaller, faster models by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Approaches vary from matching output soft-labels to imitating internal representations, attention maps, or relational structure. Distillation has been applied across modalities and tasks — NLP, vision, detection, generation, ranking, CTR prediction, graph learning, reinforcement learning and federated settings — and can be combined with architecture search and task- or domain-adaptation to produce compact models that preserve much of the teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory and compute. Practical constraints such as unavailable training data, mismatched inputs or architectures, privacy requirements, and distribution shift motivate specialized techniques including data-free distillation, student-friendly teacher training, adversarial sample generation, many-to-many layer mapping, and generative replay. Empirical results show substantial size and speed gains with modest degradation in performance in many settings, but trade-offs remain and several directions for more robust, automated and privacy-aware distillation remain active.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multi-Modal Tool for Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broadly applicable approach for compressing and adapting deep models across modalities (text, vision, graphs, speech) and deployment scenarios (edge devices, federated clients, domain shifts). Empirical evidence shows KD can improve student generalization, enable small-footprint models, and facilitate domain- or modality-transfer when combined with representation-level objectives or adversarial/contrastive methods. However, its success depends on optimization, teacher-student design, data availability, and fairness considerations. I argue that KD should be treated as a flexible framework—one that combines logit-level supervision with representation-aware objectives, domain-aware selection of teacher signals, and explicit measures to mitigate undesirable side effects (e.g., lexical errors or bias)—to reliably produce compact, high-quality models for NLP and beyond.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for transferring information from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient students. KD variants—ranging from soft-logit matching to representation- and relation-based objectives, layer mapping, online/ensemble schemes, and data-synthesis methods—have been applied across vision, NLP, translation, retrieval, federated learning, and privacy-sensitive releases. When designed with task-awareness (selecting what to distill, aligning teacher and student, and engineering the distillation data and objectives) and combined with complementary compression tools, KD often yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. However, KD is not a universal remedy: optimization challenges, teacher–student mismatch, data heterogeneity, and potential transfer of teacher errors or biases require careful mitigation. Best practice is to treat KD as a first-class element of a compression toolbox—default to distillation but tailor its form to task and deployment constraints, and combine it with architectural, data, and privacy-aware procedures to achieve robust, deployable models.

papers_seen.author: Villegas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, configurable family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains, KD reduces latency, memory, and compute while often preserving a large fraction of teacher performance. KD encompasses many targets and protocols (soft logits, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial/data‑free synthesis, multi‑teacher and self‑distillation) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies appropriate to the task and deployment constraints. Success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the availability and nature of distillation data, and mitigation of failure modes such as optimization difficulties, bias transfer, and degradation on rare phenomena. Important open directions include principled objectives, robust/private distillation under data scarcity, and specialized protocols for structured or generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Carter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for producing compact, efficient models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. KD encompasses approaches that match teacher outputs (soft logits), intermediate features or attention, relational and contrastive signals, and methods that operate with or without access to original training data. When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and matched to task- and data-specific constraints, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in parameters and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. However, effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, choice of distilled signals, data availability and preparation, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Important open problems remain in principled selection of distillation targets, reliable distillation under limited or private data, mitigation of bias transfer, and theory connecting distilled signals to student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Multifaceted Toolbox with Clear Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practically essential approach for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. KD delivers large efficiency gains and can improve generalization or robustness when combined with complementary compression methods, but it is not a single recipe: success depends on what is transferred, teacher–student alignment, data availability and quality, and constraints such as privacy or heterogeneous deployment hardware. Practical KD pipelines therefore treat distillation as a configurable toolkit—selecting objectives, data strategies, and auxiliary interventions (e.g., pruning, quantization, teacher adaptation, or student-aware design) that match the task and constraints—while explicitly addressing known failure modes such as teacher error propagation, low-frequency token degradation, and privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically driven framework for transferring predictive and representational information from large or composite teacher models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. The literature shows a broad set of distillation objectives (soft logits, intermediate feature matching, attention and relational transfer, contrastive and adversarial schemes), multiple training protocols (multi-teacher, self-distillation, data-free and synthetic-data approaches), and tight integration with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance in many settings, enable cross-modal and domain adaptation, and produce dramatic runtime and memory gains when applied with task-aware choices of signals, data, and student architectures. Important failure modes remain—teacher error propagation, capacity mismatch, data availability and heterogeneity, and fairness/privacy concerns—so best practice treats KD as a configurable toolbox that must be tailored to the task, data regime, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Park
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target supervision to a configurable toolkit including intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, online and multi-teacher protocols, data‑free synthesis, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but success is context-dependent and requires careful choices about teacher design, student capacity, data strategies, and mitigation of bias or distributional issues.

papers_seen.author: Weeks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Central, Practical, but Context-Sensitive Strategy for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practically essential set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students. KD enables deployment under strict latency, memory, and privacy constraints and supports cross-modal and domain transfer. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability and privacy, and complementary compression and training practices. Reliable compression treats distillation as a core component of a broader, task-aware pipeline rather than a standalone recipe.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical framework for transferring capabilities from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across architectures and modalities, KD methods reduce inference cost and memory while often preserving much of teacher performance; they are adaptable to settings with limited or no original training data and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and pretraining-aware workflows. Success in practice depends on careful choice of what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data and augmentation strategies, and mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer and degradation on rare phenomena. Important open directions include principled theory for diverse distillation objectives, reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, and specialized protocols for structured or generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Medina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted framework for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The literature develops a diverse toolbox—logit/soft-target transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and self-distillation, data-free or zero-shot protocols, and teacher-aware or student-aware training—often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs, multimodal) when teacher–student compatibility, data strategy, and optimization design are carefully managed; it also faces limitations arising from dataset mismatch, optimization difficulty, and propagation of teacher artifacts, especially on long-tail or low-frequency phenomena. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a configurable component of compression and deployment workflows, tuned for task constraints and complemented by safeguards for robustness, privacy, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployable systems under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD methods span soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and self-distillation, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols. Empirical evidence shows KD routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs, but reliable deployment requires task- and data-aware design, attention to teacher–student compatibility, and combination with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Central, Practical, and Responsible Strategy for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable set of techniques that enables compact models to inherit much of the performance and functionality of larger teachers. When combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and tailored to task and data constraints, KD unlocks deployment on latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained platforms while supporting modalities from language to vision and multimodal systems. However, KD is not automatic: careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate transfer of undesirable behaviors (bias, rare-token degradation) are required for responsible, robust outcomes.

Across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains, KD reduces latency, memory, and compute while often preserving a large fraction of teacher performance. KD encompasses many targets and protocols (soft logits, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial/data‑free synthesis, multi‑teacher and self‑distillation) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies appropriate to the task and deployment constraints. Success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the availability and nature of distillation data, and mitigation of failure modes such as optimization difficulties, bias transfer, and degradation on rare phenomena. Important open directions include principled objectives, robust/private distillation under data scarcity, and specialized protocols for structured or generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a practical and flexible pathway to compress large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their performance. Across NLP and other modalities, researchers have developed logit-level, representation-level, layer-wise, multi-teacher, data-free, privacy-aware, and task-aware distillation variants and combined KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows that careful choice of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data and low-frequency phenomena materially affects student quality and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression strategies transfer information from larger or differently structured models to smaller, more efficient ones. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants—matching teacher logits, intermediate representations, attention, or relational structure—enable large reductions in latency, memory, and communication while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. Practical deployment benefits from combining KD with complementary methods (pre-training, pruning, quantization, architecture search) and from careful choices about what and how to transfer, which data to use, and how to design teacher-student pairings. Key challenges remain around teacher error propagation, low-frequency/rare behavior preservation, data and domain mismatch, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment targets.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applied family of techniques for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD methods (logits, features, attention, relational, contrastive, multi‑teacher, online/self and data‑free variants) are routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation to meet deployment constraints, but their success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and alignment, and careful protocol design.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When treated as a configurable, task-aware toolkit and combined with complementary compression methods, distillation enables deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain constraints. However, its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and data strategy; it must be applied conditionally with safeguards against error and bias propagation.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. A diverse set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data-free, federated) together with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search, module replacement) enable substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD’s success is context-dependent: outcomes depend on the choice of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, student capacity, data strategy, and explicit measures to mitigate bias, low-frequency degradation, and distribution shift. Treating KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline and applying task- and data-aware design choices yields the most reliable practical results.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Practical Power, Limits, and Responsible Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and empirically validated family of techniques for compressing, adapting, and deploying deep models in constrained or sensitive settings. KD transfers information from one or more teacher models to smaller or otherwise constrained students via soft targets, intermediate-representation matching, contrastive/objective-level alignment, adversarial schemes, or synthetic-data generation. When designed carefully—choosing suitable teacher signals, aligning teacher and student capacity, integrating augmentation and complementary compression methods, and accounting for domain shift and fairness—KD routinely recovers most of a teacher's performance while enabling lower latency, smaller memory footprints, and new deployment modes (edge, federated, privacy-sensitive). However, KD is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher–student mismatch, optimization choices, and the potential transfer of undesirable properties (bias, rare-token degradation). Responsible use requires principled teacher selection, careful objective design, augmentation and sample-selection strategies, and techniques for data-free or privacy-preserving scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Bray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Task‑Aware Tool for Model Compression (with Limits and Practical Remedies)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical, versatile framework for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, or otherwise specialized students. When applied with task‑aware objectives, appropriate data strategies, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, or architecture search), KD routinely yields compact models suitable for latency- and memory-constrained deployment. However, KD is not universally sufficient: its success depends on teacher quality and compatibility with the student, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and augmentation, and mitigation of teacher artifacts. Careful protocol design—pre-training compact architectures, selecting what to distill, using effective augmentation or data synthesis, and combining KD with complementary methods—produces the most reliable results in practice.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, Practical Trade-offs, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models to meet latency, memory, privacy, and deployment constraints. The field encompasses a wide family of distillation targets and protocols (logit matching, feature- and attention-level transfer, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and self-distillation, data-free and federated variants) and is frequently combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across vision, language, recommendation, and other modalities shows that distilled students often recover much of the teacher’s performance, though outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and augmentation, and task-aware choices. Persistent challenges include handling limited or private data, transferring low-frequency/rare behaviors, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and automating teacher–student mappings for heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Challenges, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques seek to transfer knowledge from larger or more expensive models (teachers) to smaller, faster, or more interpretable students. Over the past decade these approaches have been adapted across modalities and tasks — from image classification and object detection to sequence models and large pretrained language models — and have been combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning and low-precision quantization. Empirical and theoretical work has highlighted both the practical gains of distillation (improved student generalization, reduced latency and memory, enabling deployment) and key limitations (optimization gaps, distribution mismatch, loss of certain types of information). A range of innovations — feature- and attention-based matching, layer-wise/task-aware distillation, self-distillation, data-free distillation with generative replay, teacher adaptation, and weighted/importance-aware soft labels — have been proposed to close these gaps and extend KD to settings such as domain adaptation, privacy-preserving federated learning, cross-modal transfer, and low-resource devices.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Versatile, and Bounded for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across modalities. KD provides flexible transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals), supports data-limited and privacy-sensitive regimes via synthetic- or generator-based approaches, and interoperates with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet latency and memory constraints. Nevertheless, KD is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, data and capacity matching, and explicit mitigation of bias and distribution-shift risks, so it should be used as a configurable component within broader compression and deployment pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Context‑Sensitive Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated family of techniques for producing compact models from larger teachers. KD methods range from soft-logit matching to intermediate-feature, attention, relational and adversarial objectives, and operate in offline, online, data‑free and federated regimes. While KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, its success is context dependent: teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, data strategy, and complementary compression primitives strongly determine outcomes. For reliable deployment, KD should be treated as the core of an integrated, task‑aware compression pipeline rather than a standalone cure.

papers_seen.author: Deleon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Central Benefits, Practical Limits, and Recommended Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for compressing large models into smaller, faster, or more deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD enables deployment under resource, privacy, and latency constraints, and can be adapted for task-specific compression, federated and data-free settings, low-precision inference, and bias- or domain-aware transfer. However, KD also carries practical limits: optimization gaps that prevent perfect teacher matching, transfer of teacher biases, failures on low-frequency phenomena, and sensitivity to data availability and teacher-student compatibility. To realize KD's promise practitioners should choose what signals to transfer (logits, features, relations), consider multi-teacher and confidence-weighting schemes, leverage task-aware architecture search when appropriate, and adopt specialized strategies (data-free generation, reverse distillation, counterfactual augmentation, or federated protocols) to address specific failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Context-Dependent Tools for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression provide a practical, widely applicable route to produce smaller, faster, and often more robust models from larger teachers across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks. When combined with representation-matching, contrastive objectives, multi-teacher schemes, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, its success depends on teacher quality, the data used for distillation, careful choice of what is transferred, and attention to fairness and domain-shift risks. This paper argues that KD should be treated as an essential yet context-sensitive component of model deployment pipelines, and summarizes best-practice recommendations and promising directions to make distillation reliably effective in applied settings.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically motivated family of techniques for transferring behavior from larger or ensemble teacher models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. KD methods operate at multiple levels of abstraction (output logits, intermediate features, attention and relational maps), can be adapted to scarce- or privacy-constrained data regimes, and are commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet deployment constraints. Empirically, KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance across vision and language tasks, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of transfer targets, and the availability or synthesis of appropriate distillation data. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a turnkey solution.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, pragmatic approach for producing smaller, faster, or more private models by transferring information from larger teacher models. KD succeeds widely across modalities and tasks when it is tailored to what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture search). However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful handling of bias, rare-token behavior, and domain shift. Best practice treats KD as a core element of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Jennings
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central and Practical, but Not Sufficient Alone for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and empirically effective approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD spans many transfer targets and training protocols and often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. However, KD is context-dependent: its success requires careful, task-aware choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data availability and privacy, and how to pair distillation with complementary compression tools. Treating KD as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline—rather than a single recipe—yields the most reliable path to deployable, efficient models.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression: Central, Context-Sensitive, and Best Used in Hybrid Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure across vision and NLP tasks and often recovers much of a teacher's performance, but it is not a universal cure: its reliability depends on what is distilled, how teachers and students are aligned, data availability, and complementary compression choices. Treating KD as a configurable, task-aware component within an integrated compression pipeline yields the most robust and deployable outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Indispensable but Task‑Aware
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable family of methods for compressing large models into smaller, faster, or more deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD variants have been successfully adapted across modalities and tasks, and when designed with awareness of task constraints, data availability, and student capacity, distillation yields substantial practical gains. However, KD has concrete limits—capacity mismatch, data scarcity, bias propagation, and failures on rare phenomena—that make it most effective when integrated into broader, task‑aware compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Stephens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applied strategy for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teachers into compact students. Across modalities, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while often preserving much of teacher performance. Success depends on the choice of distilled signals, teacher and student design, data availability, and integration with complementary compression techniques; awareness of practical failure modes such as capacity mismatch, optimization difficulty, distribution shift, and transferred biases is essential. This synthesis summarizes what is known about KD methods, practical integrations with other compression approaches, representative applications, common limitations, and recommended design principles for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Gordon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile set of methods for producing compact models from larger teachers. Empirical work across vision, language, and multimodal tasks shows KD can deliver large efficiency gains while often preserving much of teacher performance, but its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity, data and objective design, and complementary compression choices.
