papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression techniques transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. The literature shows a diverse set of objectives and protocols—soft-label matching, feature- and layer-level alignment, many-to-many layer mappings, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, and adversarial or generator-based sample augmentation—that together enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while trading off accuracy, robustness, and fairness. Empirical results indicate distilled students often approach teacher performance with substantially lower cost, but important limitations persist (teacher bias transfer, low-frequency token degradation, data access constraints, and capacity mismatch), motivating hybrid pipelines that combine KD with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and careful teacher–student design.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical and versatile framework that enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of the performance of large teachers. When treated as a configurable, task-aware component—combining logits, intermediate-feature matching, contrastive objectives, data augmentation, and privacy-aware techniques—distillation supports deployment across modalities and constrained devices. However, KD is not automatic: it propagates some teacher errors, can lose low-frequency or structured information, and requires careful design choices (teacher selection, objective weighting, data strategy). A principled practice that matches the distillation objective to the task, augments or tailors distillation data, and applies privacy- or domain-aware protocols yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Key
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger, often ensemble, teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods operate at the logit level, at intermediate representation and attention levels, and via relational or contrastive objectives; they are routinely combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with data strategies ranging from augmentation to data-free synthesis. Empirically, well-designed distillation pipelines can produce compact models that recover a large fraction of teacher performance, enabling deployment under latency, memory, privacy and device constraints. Success depends on choices about what and how to transfer, the quality and alignment of teacher and student, and the availability or synthesis of suitable data; important open problems remain around distribution shift, bias/fairness transfer, low-frequency behavior, and principled theoretical understanding.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. A broad and practical toolbox has been developed—output-level (soft-target) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, contrastive and relational objectives, adversarial and data-free methods, online and multi-teacher protocols, and curriculum- or architecture-aware pipelines. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often recover most teacher performance and can improve generalization when objectives, layer mappings, and data choices are well matched to student capacity and task constraints. Success requires careful design around what to transfer, how to align layers and inputs, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate bias, rare-token degradation, and teacher errors; combining KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and neural architecture search) and using task-aware curricula or projectors typically yields better accuracy–efficiency trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models. KD encompasses multiple transfer signals and training protocols and is most effective when designed with task- and deployment-awareness. While KD frequently yields large efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss, reliable deployment requires combining KD with complementary compression primitives and explicit measures to mitigate teacher imperfection, data scarcity, distribution shift, and bias propagation.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practically driven family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models by transferring information from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into compact student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods encompass matching soft logits, aligning intermediate representations and attention, transferring relational or contrastive structure, and relying on data-aware or data-free training protocols. Empirical work demonstrates that distillation often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the choice of distilled signals, and data or data-synthesis strategies. Practical application treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline combined with pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Configurable Core of Model Compression: Evidence, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an empirically validated, flexible family of methods for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger teachers into smaller students. KD routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs when the distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, and data strategies are chosen to match the task and deployment constraints. However, KD is not an automatic solution: it requires representation-aware objectives, careful handling of data and capacity mismatch, and integration with complementary compression primitives and safeguards to avoid failure modes such as bias transfer, loss of rare behaviors, and domain-shift fragility. When treated as a configurable core component of a compression pipeline rather than a plug-and-play fix, KD enables responsible, practical deployment of deep models across vision, language, multimodal, and industrial systems.

papers_seen.author: Levy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Dependent Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic set of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or specialized models by transferring behavior and representations from larger teachers. When integrated with complementary compression methods and task-aware engineering, KD routinely enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and communication while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, available data, and objective design, and it raises open challenges in robustness, privacy, and automatic student design.

papers_seen.author: Berger
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated toolbox for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger or ensembled teachers to compact students. Across modalities and domains, KD methods—when combined with task-aware data strategies and complementary compression primitives—often recover a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling deployments under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Success requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data, distribution shift, and fairness or privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Compression, Adaptation, Privacy, and Robustness in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single compression recipe: it is a flexible family of techniques that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from one set of models to another. KD enables production of compact, fast models that retain much of a larger model's performance, and it can be adapted to address domain shift, limited or private data, modality-specific constraints, and even fairness or robustness objectives. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a core component of model deployment pipelines across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models, and sequential tasks) and that careful selection among KD variants (logit, feature, ensemble, online, adversarial, data-free, teacher-free, and task-aware distillation) lets practitioners balance accuracy, latency, privacy, and fairness requirements.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Practical, but Insufficiently Complete Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has proven to be a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks. It supports multiple transfer targets (logits, features, attention, relational signals), multi-teacher and data-free setups, and integrates naturally with complementary compression methods. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and task-aware objective design. To realize KD’s full potential in real-world deployments, practitioners must treat it as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Hart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the behavior and performance of larger teachers. KD succeeds across modalities and tasks when integrated thoughtfully into compression pipelines and paired with complementary techniques, but its effectiveness is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student design, data strategy, and safeguards for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthetic Review
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants—matching teacher logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure—enable substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. Practical deployment commonly integrates KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and requires careful, task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data. Key challenges include propagation of teacher errors, degradation on low-frequency or structured outputs, data and domain mismatch, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment targets.

papers_seen.author: Meza
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad family of KD objectives and workflows—ranging from soft-logit matching to intermediate-feature alignment, multi‑teacher and self‑distillation, data‑free and adversarial approaches, and projector or curriculum-based engineering—has been developed and applied across vision and language tasks. Distillation enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints but is not universally guaranteed: outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful choice of transfer signals and training procedures. The practical consensus is to treat KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Woods
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, Practical Guidance, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teachers into compact students. KD methods operate at multiple levels—from soft-label (logit) matching to feature-, attention-, and relation-level transfers—and have been adapted to many training and deployment protocols (offline teacher→student, online/co‑distillation, self‑distillation, multi‑teacher, data‑free, and federated schemes). Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, retrieval, and recommendation shows that KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, and distillation data are properly matched. In practice, KD is most effective when used as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline that includes complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, pretraining, data augmentation, and careful layer alignment. Remaining challenges include handling teacher biases and errors, preserving low-frequency or minority behaviors, operating under data absence or strict privacy constraints, and automating teacher–student design for heterogeneous deployment targets.

papers_seen.author: Hunter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. The literature provides a diverse toolkit—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate feature and attention imitation, contrastive and relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or synthetic-data approaches—together with engineering practices that pair KD with pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data/curriculum strategies. Empirical results show KD often preserves much of the teacher’s performance across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, yet important challenges remain around teacher–student mismatch, data scarcity and privacy, robustness and fairness, and reliable transfer of low-frequency or structured behaviors. Continued progress centers on designing what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to integrate KD into end-to-end compression pipelines for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Lester
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically important family of techniques for producing compact student models from larger teacher models. Across vision, language, multimodal, and constrained-deployment settings, KD uses diverse transfer targets and training protocols to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while often preserving a large fraction of teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals, student capacity, and data strategies to task and deployment constraints and on integrating KD with complementary compression methods and privacy-aware procedures.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad family of distillation objectives—ranging from soft-logit matching to feature-, attention- and layer-wise alignment, relational/contrastive signals, adversarial and data-free sample synthesis, and meta- or multi-teacher schemes—has been developed and applied across vision, language, retrieval, graph, and federated settings. In practice, KD is most effective when combined with task- and architecture-aware design choices and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Remaining challenges include teacher–student mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, limited or private data, and optimization stability; proposed remedies emphasize task-aware filtering of teacher signals, learned teacher adaptation, layer mapping strategies, and data-synthesis or privacy-aware protocols.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Chang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teachers to smaller student models. KD operates at multiple levels (soft targets, intermediate representations, structured signals) and combines naturally with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, privacy, and deployment constraints. Effectiveness is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and optimization design; addressing these practical dimensions is central to reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, but Imperfect Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for producing smaller, faster models from large teachers across vision, language, graph, and generative settings. KD supports deployment on constrained hardware, domain adaptation, improved interpretability, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware techniques. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on teacher quality, data and augmentation choices, objective design, and handling of distributional or architectural mismatch. Careful engineering and complementary compression techniques are necessary to realize KD's benefits in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Tool for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured from a technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones into a broad set of methods that address efficiency, domain adaptation, privacy, robustness, fairness, and cross-modal transfer. By moving beyond simple logits matching to layer- and feature-level alignment, multi-teacher schemes, data-free and few-shot settings, and meta-learned teachers, distillation can both preserve performance and add functional guarantees (e.g., robustness, fairness) that are crucial for real-world deployment. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered a foundational component of model compression pipelines and of strategies for adapting large pre-trained models to constrained, specialized, or sensitive applications.

papers_seen.author: Carpenter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. KD reliably reduces latency and memory while often preserving much of teacher performance across vision, language, speech, and generative tasks, but its effectiveness is conditional on teacher quality, data used for distillation, and architectural alignment. For deployment-ready compression, KD should be treated as a cornerstone technique that is combined with task-aware design choices and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to close remaining optimization and generalization gaps.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their accuracy. Empirical results across vision, language, retrieval, detection, generative models, and distributed settings show KD can close much of the performance gap between large and compact models, but best outcomes require tailoring what and how knowledge is transferred and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques and domain-aware procedures.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a narrow training trick into a broad, practical paradigm for compressing and adapting large deep models to resource- and data-constrained deployment settings. A rich family of KD formulations — from logit matching and feature imitation to adversarial, data-free, and online schemes — together with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and teacher ensembles) enables substantial reductions in memory and latency while largely preserving model quality. However, KD is not universally effective out-of-the-box: its benefits and risks depend on task characteristics, data availability, teacher–student compatibility, and deliberate choices of what and how to transfer. When practitioners treat KD as a toolkit of targeted strategies and validate choices against task constraints, it yields the best trade-offs between efficiency, robustness, and fidelity to the original model.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, practical framework for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient students for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. A diverse toolkit of distillation objectives and protocols—ranging from soft-label (logit) matching to intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi-/self-distillation, and data-free protocols—has been developed and applied across vision, language, speech, graphs, and multimodal tasks. KD is most effective when integrated into task-aware pipelines that align teacher and student architectures, choose appropriate transfer signals, and combine distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) while explicitly addressing limitations such as distribution shift, teacher-induced biases, and degradation on low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically supported approach for producing compact models that retain much of the predictive power of larger teachers while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD supports many transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational constraints), accommodates data-limited and data-free settings, and combines effectively with complementary compression techniques such as pruning and quantization. At the same time, reliable deployment requires attention to teacher quality, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and fairness or robustness considerations. When applied with these considerations in mind, KD is often the most practical and flexible first-line strategy for model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of their performance. Across vision, speech, graphs, recommender systems, and NLP, KD has diversified from the original logits-based teacher-student protocol into feature- and representation-based objectives, data-free and generative approaches, multi- and ensemble-teacher schemes, online and collaborative strategies, and task-aware adaptations. Empirical work shows distilled students often reclaim much of teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, and data used for transfer are properly matched; however, optimization issues, data heterogeneity, and the risk of propagating teacher biases remain practical challenges. Complementary techniques—pruning, quantization, architecture search, pretraining, and careful layer alignment—regularly improve outcomes and are recommended for deployment in constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Beyond in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a compression trick into a broad set of techniques that enable efficient deployment, cross-modal transfer, federated and privacy-preserving learning, and improved generalization across domains. Empirical results across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs) show that KD can substantially reduce model size and latency while retaining most of the teacher performance. However, the success of KD depends on careful choices — teacher quality, what to distill (outputs, features, internal representations), data availability and augmentation, and the loss or alignment mechanism — and recent work proposes multiple refinements (multi-teacher schemes, adversarial critics, projector modules, teacher-free variants) that mitigate known failure modes. The balance of empirical evidence and theoretical analyses indicates that KD is both practically indispensable for many compression tasks and a fertile area for research on how knowledge should be measured, transferred, and regularized.

papers_seen.author: Oconnell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across modalities and tasks. When designed as part of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline — integrating pretraining, multi-signal transfer (logits, features, relational signals), data strategies, and compatible architecture choices — KD can preserve most teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, its effectiveness is conditional: it depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the distilled signals and data, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases or rare-case failures. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the practical core of modern model-compression toolkits, outlines concrete mechanisms by which it helps, surveys domain- and task-specific variants that address common failure modes, and summarizes actionable design principles for robust, responsible deployment.

papers_seen.author: Barrett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, and Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. Across tasks and modalities, KD variants transfer outputs or internal signals to reduce model size and latency while often preserving most task performance. Practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures and capacities, how to handle data (real, augmented, or synthetic), and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques. When treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline, KD enables deployable models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints—but it is not a standalone panacea and requires task‑aware engineering to mitigate failure modes such as propagated teacher errors, distribution shift, and degraded long‑tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Path for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from teacher models. Across tasks and modalities, distillation methods—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature and structure-preserving objectives—enable deployable models that retain much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory use, and communication cost. Distillation also serves as a flexible substrate for addressing domain adaptation, lifelong learning, robustness, low-precision deployment, and generator compression. However, realizing these benefits in practice requires careful design choices around what to transfer, how to map layers and representations, how to handle limited or private teacher data, and how to mitigate bias or robustness loss.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information at multiple levels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention/relational structure, or synthesized examples—and can be organized in diverse protocols (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, multi‑teacher, self‑distillation, and data‑free regimes). When combined with complementary compression tools such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, KD routinely produces compact models that recover a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and communication costs. However, KD’s success is strongly context dependent: it depends on teacher quality and calibration, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability and match of distillation data (or quality of synthetic surrogates), and careful objective and pipeline design to avoid propagating teacher errors or degrading long‑tail behaviour. Practical deployment therefore treats KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline, not a universal panacea.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible, and widely applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of their performance. Across domains and tasks—language modeling and translation, recommendation, graph learning, vision, continual and domain adaptation, and resource-constrained deployment—KD enables trade-offs between accuracy, latency, memory, privacy, and train-time complexity. Variants such as feature mimicking, self- and teacher-free distillation, ensemble and online distillation, data-free and privacy-aware schemes, and task- or domain-aware adaptations extend KD’s applicability. At the same time, careful choice of training targets, treatment of low-frequency phenomena, and consideration of the teacher-student mismatch are necessary to avoid transferring teacher errors and to realize the full benefits of distillation.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Aware Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically supported approach for reducing model size and latency across vision, language, multimodal, and graph domains. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and selection, and mitigation of propagated errors or bias. Best practice treats KD as a central but context‑sensitive element of integrated compression pipelines that include pruning, quantization, architecture search, data strategies, and task-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Armstrong
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller student models so that compact models can approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, privacy, and deployment constraints. Empirical evidence shows KD routinely yields large efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss across modalities, but its success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment and capacity, data availability (including data-free methods), and careful mitigation of transferred biases and other failure modes. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core of a broader compression pipeline that integrates complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for transferring predictive capacity from large, high-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). A wide range of KD objectives and protocols have been developed — from matching teacher logits to mimicking internal features, adversarially chosen samples, and data-free or zero-shot synthesis — and these are routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can recover much of the teacher's performance and, when carefully engineered, support robustness, domain adaptation, privacy-preserving releases, and practical latency- or memory-constrained deployment. At the same time, KD’s effectiveness depends on what is transferred, teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and optimization choices, leaving open practical challenges around heterogeneous architectures, distribution shift, and preserving fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a versatile, multi-faceted toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most of a teacher’s accuracy while producing meaningful reductions in parameters, latency, memory, and communication cost. However, KD is not automatic: its success depends on matching distilled signals to the task and student capacity, selecting or synthesizing appropriate data, and combining distillation with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical pipelines treat KD as a configurable component within a broader compression and deployment strategy that explicitly addresses teacher imperfection, distribution shift, rare behaviors, privacy, and architecture heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Horton

papers_seen.author: Rasmussen

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression comprise a diverse set of techniques to produce smaller, faster, or more private models by transferring information from larger or auxiliary models. Practical work demonstrates benefits across vision, multimodal, graph, and NLP tasks, while theoretical analyses connect distillation to label smoothing, ensemble behavior, and bias–variance tradeoffs. Open challenges include aligning heterogeneous inputs and modalities, preserving robustness and privacy, and handling low-resource or low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches

Across vision, language, multimodal, and federated settings, researchers have applied KD for inference speedup, deployment on resource-constrained devices, privacy-preserving model release, and enhanced robustness or interpretability. Methods vary from standard teacher–student soft-label supervision to data-free distillation, adversarially chosen boundary samples, many-to-many layer mappings, generative replay, and architecture-aware compression. Empirical results show KD can yield large efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss when combined with task-aware design, careful sample selection, and appropriate optimization; challenges remain around distributional mismatch, low-frequency token handling, heterogeneous architectures, and privacy/validation in data-free scenarios. Emerging directions include task-adaptive compressed models, joint optimization of pruning and KD, federated/distilled learning across heterogeneous devices, and cross-modal distillation for generative capabilities.

However, its practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and distribution, and the design of distillation objectives; consequently KD should be treated as a configurable component that is combined with complementary compression techniques and deployment-aware safeguards.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques provide a practical path to deploy high-performing deep models under resource, latency, privacy, or domain constraints. Across vision and language, researchers have explored teacher-student training, intermediate-layer alignment, data- and label-space manipulations, data-free or few-shot settings, and architecture-aware compression. These techniques can preserve much of a teacher's performance while yielding smaller, faster models, and they can be combined with pruning, architecture search, or ensemble compression. KD also intersects with concerns about fairness, generalization, and privacy, and its effectiveness depends on design choices such as the form of distilled targets, data augmentation, and the match between teacher, student, and task.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Conditional, and Integrative Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential method for producing compact models from larger teachers across modalities in deep learning and NLP. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can transfer predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and inductive biases that yield substantial gains in latency, memory, and often accuracy. However, KD has concrete failure modes—teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity, bias transfer, and distribution shift—that limit its effectiveness when used alone. The strongest, most reliable outcomes arise when KD is treated as a configurable core of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline that combines careful teacher engineering, targeted distillation signals, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compressing large models for deployment across domains and modalities. When designed with task-awareness (choice of distilled signal, teacher selection, and training scheme), KD can preserve accuracy while materially improving latency, memory, and privacy characteristics. Best results arise from combining multiple KD techniques (logit, feature, layer-wise, adversarial, and ensemble-based) chosen to match the task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Sheppard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically grounded approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of teacher performance. Across modalities and tasks, KD variants—soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, and data-free or adversarial synthesis—enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints and integrate with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD is highly effective when treated as a task-aware toolkit: careful choice of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and combination with other compression primitives produces practical, deployable models. However, KD is not a panacea; its limitations (teacher errors, capacity mismatch, data scarcity, bias transfer, and distribution shift) require explicit mitigation, specialized protocols, and continued research into robust, privacy-preserving, and automated distillation methods.

papers_seen.author: Espinoza
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly validated, practical family of techniques for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, graph, and reinforcement-learning settings. A diverse toolkit—soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and self-teaching, data-free synthesis, and architecture-aware adaptations—enables large reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often preserving most teacher performance. Success in practice depends on choices about which signals to transfer, teacher–student alignment, availability and selection of data (or pseudo-data), and complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Remaining scientific and engineering challenges include principled theory connecting distilled signals to student generalization, robust transfer across heterogeneous architectures and non-iid data, mitigation of transferred biases and degradation on rare outputs, and reliable privacy-preserving or federated protocols.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a broad set of techniques to compress large or ensemble models into smaller, faster, or more deployable models while preserving performance. Research spans logits-based distillation, feature and representation matching, intermediate-layer alignment, adversarial and self-supervised schemes, curriculum and online protocols, and task-adaptive or privacy-preserving variants. Practical work demonstrates successful applications across NLP (including compressing BERT), vision, graph learning, retrieval, object detection, and large-scale distributed training, with ongoing research focused on teacher design, data augmentation, and robustness under limited or heterogeneous data.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context-Dependent Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their predictive performance. KD operates at multiple levels—from soft-target (logit) supervision to representation- and layer-wise alignment—and integrates naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-augmentation or curriculum strategies. Empirical evidence across vision, language, generative models, and retrieval shows distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher accuracy and can add benefits such as improved generalization or interpretability when applied carefully. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, optimization choices, and explicit handling of teacher biases and distribution shift. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component in a broader compression pipeline, chosen and tuned to the task, data availability, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Haynes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Patterns, Practical Strategies, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used set of techniques for transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while preserving much of task performance. The literature shows a broad toolkit—soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and layer-mapping objectives, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and multi-teacher or self-distillation protocols—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical evidence indicates KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can improve low-precision and deployment behavior, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful alignment of objectives and training procedures. Open problems remain around robustness, distribution shift, low-frequency behavior, fairness, and principled design of teacher–student pairings and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.
