papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Configurable Core of Practical Model-Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically supported approach for converting large teacher models into compact, deployable students across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks. Treated as a configurable toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD produces favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when combined with complementary compression primitives and with intentional choices about what and how to transfer. At the same time, KD is not automatic: reliable deployment requires addressing teacher–student mismatch, data limitations, and the risk of propagating undesirable behaviors. I argue that KD should be adopted as a central, context‑sensitive component of hybrid compression pipelines whose design is driven by task constraints and by explicit mitigation strategies for known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Rivas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, enable deployment under resource or privacy constraints, and sometimes improve calibration, robustness, or task adaptation. The field has evolved from logits-based soft-target training to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free approaches, multi-teacher and online schemes, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity and task constraints, handling limited or mismatched data, and explicitly addressing risks such as transferred biases or privacy leakage. KD is most effective when treated as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a single turnkey algorithm.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across modalities and tasks, practitioners transfer logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or decision-boundary information and combine KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation) to meet latency, memory, privacy, and domain constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students often recover most teacher performance and, in some cases, match or exceed teachers when distillation is paired with careful teacher design, layer mapping, and data or training schedules. Major limitations remain in imperfect belief matching, distribution shift, handling low-frequency phenomena, heterogeneous or privacy-constrained data, and principled teacher selection—areas where methodological and theoretical progress continues to be needed.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and highly practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD techniques range from simple soft-target matching to representation- and task-aware objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-augmentation and data-free protocols, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is effective across modalities and tasks but is not a silver bullet: its success depends on teacher quality, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and augmentation, architecture alignment, and explicit handling of biases and distribution shift. Treated as a core component within an integrated compression pipeline and designed with task constraints in mind, KD yields reliable tradeoffs between efficiency and fidelity for deployment in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression (but Not a Standalone Cure)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable technique for producing compact models from larger teachers. KD supports many transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, and data-free variants), and combinations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across vision, language, retrieval, detection, and healthcare shows KD routinely enables substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and careful objective and architecture design. Best practice treats KD as the central, configurable element of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline that explicitly addresses data scarcity, distribution shift, privacy, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broad, practical toolkit for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger networks. Across vision, language, graphs, speech, and generative modeling, researchers transfer information via softened output distributions, intermediate-feature matching, relational and attention maps, and many-to-many layer alignment. Variants address resource heterogeneity, data unavailability, privacy, robustness, and fairness. Empirical and analytic work shows that distillation combines information transfer with regularization effects, but its success depends on design choices (what to transfer, teacher quality, data or pseudo-data, and alignment losses). State-of-the-art practice mixes logits-based loss with feature- or representation-level objectives, task-aware augmentations, and architecture- or training-aware modifications to obtain favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs in deployment.

papers_seen.author: Mcintyre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models so they run under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. KD methods operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational/contrastive structures, adversarial or data-free synthesis) and are routinely combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and multilingual tasks shows that properly designed distillation pipelines often recover a large fraction of teacher performance, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and alignment, data availability or synthesis, and careful choice of objectives and layer mappings. Important open problems include robust data-free distillation, principled transfer choices for heterogeneous architectures, and controls for fairness and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broad family of techniques that make large, high-performing models practical for deployment by transferring behavior, representations, or decision structure to smaller models. KD succeeds across modalities and tasks when combined with appropriate supervision signals, data practices, and architectural alignment, but it also has important failure modes—propagated teacher errors, sensitivity to data distribution and teacher quality, and limits when student capacity is insufficient. I argue KD should be treated as a foundational component of model-compression pipelines, applied thoughtfully and in combination with complementary methods (augmentation, pruning/quantization, privacy mechanisms, and federated protocols) to realize robust, efficient systems for real-world NLP and deep-learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Brooks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically effective approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers. When treated as a configurable component of a compression pipeline and adapted to teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of a teacher's performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: its effectiveness depends on signal selection, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and integration with complementary compression methods; responsible use requires mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, low‑frequency degradation, and privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Contextual Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective, broadly applicable set of methods for producing smaller, faster, and deployment-ready models by transferring information from large teacher models into compact students. KD techniques range from soft-label (logit) matching to intermediate-feature and relational objectives, and they have been adapted to settings with limited or no original training data, to multi-teacher or online schemes, and to combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. While KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can improve interpretability or privacy-aware deployment, its success depends on task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data and distributional constraints. Consequently, KD is best treated as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline rather than as a plug-and-play cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Conditional Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and practical set of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. KD succeeds by transferring rich forms of information — soft logits, intermediate features, attention patterns, relational or contrastive structure, and even synthesized data — and by being combined with complementary compression tools such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, KD is not an automatic remedy: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and privacy constraints, and defenses against transferring teacher errors or low-frequency phenomena. Treating KD as a configurable, task-aware component within a broader compression pipeline, and adopting practices such as layer- and task-aware objectives, multi-teacher confidence weighting, adversarial or decision-boundary sample generation, and data-aware synthesis or augmentation, yields the most reliable trade-offs between efficiency and fidelity. Remaining research directions include principled guidance for selecting which signals to transfer, robust privacy-preserving distillation, and automated, deployment-aware distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Flexible, but Not Panacea Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students and for transferring task- or modality-specific capabilities. KD supports many transfer targets and training protocols and can be combined with pruning, quantization, pretraining, and data synthesis to meet deployment constraints. However, reliable outcomes require careful teacher–student design, attention to data and privacy constraints, and targeted solutions for failure modes such as distribution shift, optimization mismatch, and preserved low-frequency behavior.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context-Sensitive Path for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a proven and versatile technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When designed around appropriate transfer targets, teacher–student alignment, and data regimes, KD frequently enables substantial reductions in size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. However, its effectiveness depends on task and deployment constraints, and KD must often be combined with complementary methods and task-aware design to avoid failure modes and to meet real-world requirements.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques are widely used to produce smaller, faster models while preserving much of the performance of large teachers. Approaches vary from matching final logits to transferring internal representations, attention maps, or layer-wise information, and they are applied across modalities including NLP, vision, speech, and reinforcement learning. Practical extensions address multi-teacher setups, data-free scenarios, domain adaptation, quantization, and architecture-aware compression; remaining challenges include handling heterogeneous architectures, data heterogeneity, fairness, and reliably preserving inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Analyses, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing and adapting large neural models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained models while retaining much of their performance. A diverse set of KD approaches operate at the level of final outputs (logits), intermediate features, layer relations, or via adversarial and data-generation mechanisms. KD has been adapted across modalities and tasks — from NLP transformer compression to GAN and speech-model compression, cross-modal transfer, federated settings, and domain-specific applications — and interacts strongly with concerns about robustness, fairness, and transfer of inductive biases. Empirical and theoretical work has clarified when and why various KD variants help, and highlights open challenges in data heterogeneity, teacher-student mismatch, and automatic discovery of compact architectures.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: This synthesis reviews empirical and methodological advances in knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques as applied across vision, language, generative models, retrieval, recommender systems, federated and lifelong learning. It summarizes mechanisms for transferring teacher knowledge to smaller students (soft labels, intermediate representations, curriculum and selective sample strategies), practical challenges (data availability, teacher cost, domain shift, privacy, and bias), and targeted solutions (data-free distillation, fast label generation, multi-teacher and domain-adaptive schemes, self-distillation, and distillation-aware pruning). The goal is to map what the provided literature reports about when distillation helps, when it can hurt, and which strategies are effective for different settings and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: The Efficacy and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into efficient students across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models, and reinforcement learning). Empirical work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance while offering substantial inference speedups and parameter reductions, and can be enhanced by targeted techniques (data augmentation, intermediate-layer matching, multi-teacher schedules, contrastive objectives, and meta-learning). However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends strongly on distillation procedure, data complexity, teacher–student alignment, and training dynamics. Practical deployment requires selecting distillation objectives and data strategies that address robustness, limited-data regimes, privacy/federation, and modality-specific needs.

papers_seen.author: Ballard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile framework for compressing large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD encompasses a range of transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data‑free), and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and multimodal settings shows KD frequently recovers much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, and data strategies. Practical deployment treats KD as a configurable, task-aware component of broader compression pipelines and adopts safeguards for robustness, privacy, and low-frequency or long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Gomez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and NLP, KD spans logits/soft-label matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher schemes, data‑free and privacy-aware protocols, and self- or teacher-free variants. When combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and designed with attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data strategy, and task constraints, KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss. Practical deployment requires task-aware choices, careful alignment of teacher and student, and explicit mitigations for distributional mismatch, rare-token behavior, and transferred biases; important open problems remain in principled theory, robust/private data-free distillation, and heterogeneous architecture transfer.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or specialized student models. KD methods—ranging from soft-target (logit) transfer to intermediate feature and attention matching, many-to-many layer mappings, adversarial ensemble compression, and privacy-aware protocols—enable deployment under compute, memory, latency, and privacy constraints while often improving student generalization. Practical success depends on aligning teacher signals to student capacity and task needs, choosing or synthesizing suitable data, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Key challenges remain in handling teacher imperfection and bias, data- and domain-shift, low-frequency/structured outputs, and providing principled guarantees for fairness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential, Versatile, and Context-Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical set of techniques for transferring behavior and representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques — spanning soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate-representation matching, adversarial or data-free synthesis, and teacher-aware or multi-teacher strategies — repeatedly enable large reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on task and data properties, teacher–student alignment, optimization, and deployment constraints, and it works best when combined with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A First‑Class, Task‑Aware Tool for Model Compression (but Not a Panacea)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and highly effective approach for producing compact, efficient models across modalities and tasks. Empirical evidence shows KD often preserves most teacher performance while delivering large gains in latency, memory, and deployability; however, its success depends on task-aware design choices, data availability, and careful mitigation of teacher artifacts. KD should be treated as a first‑order component of any compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques when necessary.

papers_seen.author: Carpenter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. KD reliably reduces latency and memory while often preserving much of teacher performance across vision, language, speech, and generative tasks, but its effectiveness is conditional on teacher quality, data used for distillation, and architectural alignment. For deployment-ready compression, KD should be treated as a cornerstone technique that is combined with task-aware design choices and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to close remaining optimization and generalization gaps.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. The methods range from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate features, attention maps, and relational or contrastive structures, and they operate in offline, online, multi-teacher, cross-modal, and data-constrained regimes. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful, task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align layers, and how to handle limited or private data. While KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, open challenges remain in teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift, robustness and fairness transfer, data-free/privacy-preserving distillation, and principled selection of distilled signals.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of the Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: This synthesis summarizes empirical findings, methodological variants, use-cases, limitations, and practical recommendations for knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques in deep learning and NLP. Drawing solely on the provided studies, it highlights common transfer targets and training regimes, domain- and task-specific adaptations, and recurring failure modes, and offers guidance on when and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of the Provided Literature
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under constraints of latency, memory, compute, or privacy. Methods range from matching soft logits to imitating intermediate features, attention maps, and relational structure, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and specialized data strategies. KD has enabled strong empirical gains across modalities and tasks (classification, generation, translation, graph learning, and recommender systems) but requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate transfer of undesirable behaviors. Key practical themes include selecting appropriate distillation signals, handling teacher–student capacity and architecture mismatches, designing or synthesizing data when originals are unavailable, and integrating KD with complementary compression methods to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Howard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature documents a broad set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational and contrastive signals), protocols (offline, online/mutual, self-distillation, multi-teacher), and data strategies (real-data, augmented, synthetic, and data-free/generative approaches). Practically effective KD requires task- and data-aware choices—what signals to transfer, how to align architectures and layers, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to combine KD with complementary compression tools such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. While KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can improve robustness or generalization when well designed, predictable failure modes remain (teacher–student capacity mismatch, teacher error/bias transfer, poor modeling of low-frequency phenomena, distribution shift, and data/privacy limitations), motivating targeted mitigations and continued theoretical and empirical work.

papers_seen.author: Perkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a flexible, task-aware family of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, efficient students while often preserving much of teacher performance. KD encompasses a range of distilled signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational structure), training protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data-free and few-shot), and data strategies (authentic, augmented, synthetic, or generated replay). Empirical work across vision, speech, language, graphs, and multimodal tasks shows that KD produces meaningful efficiency–accuracy trade-offs when teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and signal selection are aligned; however, KD is not automatic and faces limits from capacity mismatch, teacher artifacts, low-frequency or structured outputs, data heterogeneity, and fairness/privacy concerns. Best practice treats KD as a configurable toolbox that is integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with safeguards for robustness, privacy, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Thomas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Contextual Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across modalities. Empirical and methodological work shows KD frequently preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and inference cost. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architectural alignment, data availability and design, and explicit mitigation of transferred errors, biases, and rare-case degradation. For robust, production-ready compression pipelines, KD should be treated as the central mechanism embedded within task-aware practices that include complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful teacher–student engineering, and data- and fairness-aware protocols.

papers_seen.author: Cooke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision, language, speech, detection, recommendation, and multimodal tasks, KD methods—ranging from soft-logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, adversarial and contrastive objectives, data-free synthesis, and online or multi-teacher protocols—enable substantial efficiency gains while often preserving much of teacher performance. Success depends on choices about what to transfer, data strategy, teacher–student alignment, and complementary compression (e.g., pruning, quantization, or architecture search). Practical deployments use task-aware adaptations, confidence- or curriculum-based weighting, and privacy- or federated-aware designs; remaining challenges include teacher–student mismatch, limited or private data, distribution shift, rare-output transfer, and principled theory for optimal transfer.

papers_seen.author: Knight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated toolkit for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact students. KD methods span output-level soft-target matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and online/self-distillation protocols. In practice, KD is most effective when treated as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline that also uses pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies; its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases and rare-case failures.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, often ensemble or pre-trained, teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD includes matching teacher outputs (soft logits), imitating intermediate representations, transferring attention or relational structures, and using multi-teacher, online, self-, or data-free protocols. In practice KD is combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware design to enable deployment under compute, memory, latency, and privacy constraints. While KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and can improve student generalization, its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and match, and careful choice of distillation signals; persistent challenges include optimization gaps, distribution shift, low-frequency/rare-case degradation, bias transfer, and federated or heterogeneous-device constraints. Ongoing work focuses on principled objectives, layer-mapping strategies, privacy- and data-aware distillation, and robust, task-aware pipelines for production deployment.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, practical family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models to compact student models. A rich design space—what information to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive signals), how to schedule training (offline, online, progressive, or data-free), and how to combine KD with pruning, quantization, or architecture search—makes KD applicable across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains. Empirical evidence shows KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling deployment under compute, memory, and privacy constraints, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability (or synthesis), and explicit attention to robustness, bias, and distribution shift. Best results treat KD as an adaptable toolkit that must be tailored to task, data regime, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Foundational, Context-Dependent, and Best Deployed as Part of an Integrated Compression Toolkit
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful set of methods for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD variants—from logits and feature matching to self-, multi-teacher, and data-free protocols—have been shown to reduce model size and latency while often retaining much of teacher performance across vision, language, graph, generative, and detection tasks. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, what is transferred, and interactions with other training practices. To realize KD’s practical value one should design distillation around task objectives and deployment constraints and combine it with complementary compression and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. The literature provides a broad toolkit of distillation targets and protocols, and shows KD is effective across classification, language modeling, translation, detection, recommendation, and retrieval when combined with task-aware design and complementary compression methods. Practical success depends on student capacity, teacher quality and alignment, data availability or synthesis, and integration with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Open problems include principled theory, robust transfer under distribution shift or privacy constraints, heterogeneous architectures, and preserving rare or structured outputs.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

Empirical work shows KD can yield compact models that retain much teacher performance, but success depends on careful selection of what and how to transfer, data availability, and the match between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis from Selected Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and deployment-ready students while retaining much of their performance. papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression strategies transfer information from larger or differently structured models to smaller, more efficient ones. papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Practicalities, and Open Challenges

Remaining practical limits include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, degradation on low-frequency phenomena, and reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints; current remedies emphasize task-aware objective design, multi-signal supervision, teacher adaptation, and integration with other compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Work
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing and accelerating deep models by transferring knowledge from larger (teacher) models to smaller (student) models. Beyond straightforward parameter reduction, KD is used to improve student generalization, robustness, interpretability, domain adaptation, continual learning, and to enable deployment in latency- or resource-constrained settings. The literature shows a wide variety of KD objectives (logit/soft-label matching, feature imitation, relational losses), training protocols (multi-teacher, curriculum, adversarial or zero-shot data generation, teacher-free/self-distillation), and application-specific adaptations (detection, retrieval, GANs, speech, lipreading, 3D vision, recommender systems, and NLP). Empirical results demonstrate that carefully designed distillation pipelines can recover much of teacher performance and in some cases surpass teachers on efficiency-accuracy trade-offs, but raise challenges including heterogeneous teacher-student alignment, data availability, preserving low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors, and transferring robustness and domain-general knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Hicks

The field encompasses a diverse set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational maps, contrastive signals), multiple training protocols (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, self-distillation, multi-teacher and ensemble schemes), and data strategies that include data-driven, synthetic, and data-free approaches. KD is routinely integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and applied across modalities (NLP, vision, speech, generative models, recommender and graph systems). Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the distillation signal and its alignment, and the availability and curation of data; remaining challenges include preserving low-frequency behaviors, avoiding transfer of teacher biases, and maintaining robustness under distribution shift and limited-data regimes. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an overall compression pipeline with task-aware signal selection, careful teacher–student co-design, and targeted mitigations for privacy, fairness, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques form a diverse set of methods for producing smaller, faster, or more deployable models by transferring knowledge from larger or specialized models. Approaches span from simple soft-label supervision to richer transfers of internal representations, intermediate-layer mappings, attention-guided projections, adversarial feature alignment, and task- or device-aware compression. KD is used across domains—image classification, detection (2D and 3D), recommendation/CTR, language model compression, federated and heterogeneous-device learning, and reinforcement learning—and is frequently combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or curriculum strategies. Recent work examines theoretical aspects (e.g., bias–variance tradeoffs and statistical interactions with data augmentation), practical design choices (teacher-student layer alignment, many-to-many mappings, ensemble teachers), and extensions that address privacy, fairness, and low-data regimes. Despite strong empirical success, open problems remain in understanding when particular KD variants best transfer generalization, how to measure and mitigate transferred biases, and how to optimally combine KD with other compression primitives for different constraints.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, more efficient student models. Across vision, language, speech, and other modalities KD routinely yields favorable efficiency–accuracy trade-offs when it is treated as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline. Practical success requires choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to manage or synthesize distillation data, and how to combine KD with complementary compression methods. Important open problems include reliably preserving robustness and long‑tail behaviors, principled teacher–student co‑design, and safe use under privacy and fairness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across deep learning and NLP. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations using a variety of signals and training protocols, and when combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware choices it enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is context dependent: its success hinges on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of transferred errors, robustness deficits, and fairness or privacy issues. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a stand‑alone cure.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their capabilities. KD enables deployment across modalities and constrained environments, and empirical work shows it can approach teacher performance when combined with complementary techniques. However, KD is not a universal solution: it can propagate teacher errors and biases, struggle under data scarcity or mismatch, and require careful choices of distilled targets, architectures, and training schedules. To realize KD's benefits in production and research settings, practitioners should pair distillation with targeted remedies—representation-aware objectives, data-and-curriculum strategies, ensemble or adversarial schemes, and fairness or privacy interventions—tailored to task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Mendoza
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Effects, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used, flexible framework for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact students. KD encompasses a range of transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive signals) and protocols (offline, online, multi-teacher, data-free, and curriculum-driven). Empirical work demonstrates KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute, but its success is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals, data availability or synthesis, and integration with complementary compression tools such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical deployment therefore treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone cure-all. Key open directions include principled selection of signals to transfer, robust privacy-preserving distillation, automation of deployment-aware pipelines, and reliable compression of large transformer and generative models.

papers_seen.author: Juarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Across vision, language, graphs, multimodal tasks and specialized settings (e.g., 3D detection, ranking, medical imaging), KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how teacher and student are aligned, and how data or synthetic alternatives are used; KD is most effective when used as a configurable component combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware training strategies.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Benefits, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring predictive and representational information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy. KD has been adapted to diverse transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational maps), multi-teacher schemes, data-free or few-shot regimes, and domain- or task-adaptive pipelines. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful teacher–student design, KD routinely yields large reductions in model size and runtime while preserving most of the teacher's performance. However, distillation is not automatic: practitioner attention is needed to address teacher selection, data availability and distribution shift, capacity mismatch, low-frequency behavior, and risk of transferring biases or teacher artifacts.
