papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Webb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Toolkit for Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably reduces model size and inference cost by transferring information from larger teachers to smaller students, but its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to train, and how to integrate complementary compression methods. When designed as part of a task-aware pipeline—with attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data strategies, and privacy or fairness constraints—KD yields deployable models that retain much of teacher performance; treated naively it can propagate errors and fail under data- or capacity-mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Espinoza
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly validated, practical family of techniques for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, graph, and reinforcement-learning settings. A diverse toolkit—soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and self-teaching, data-free synthesis, and architecture-aware adaptations—enables large reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often preserving most teacher performance. Success in practice depends on choices about which signals to transfer, teacher–student alignment, availability and selection of data (or pseudo-data), and complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Remaining scientific and engineering challenges include principled theory connecting distilled signals to student generalization, robust transfer across heterogeneous architectures and non-iid data, mitigation of transferred biases and degradation on rare outputs, and reliable privacy-preserving or federated protocols.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied framework for compressing large models, improving generalization, and transferring capabilities across modalities and deployment constraints. Research spans teacher-student paradigms (including multi-teacher and self-distillation), data-free and zero-shot distillation, task-adaptive compression, and applications to specialized tasks (detection, retrieval, translation, multimodal learning, federated settings, and graph problems). Empirical work shows KD can yield large speed and size gains while retaining much of the teacher's performance, but also exposes important limitations tied to optimization, data used for distillation, and potential bias transfer. Recent methods address these limitations via curriculum scheduling, confidence- or reinforcement-based teacher weighting, task-adaptive architecture search, domain- and modality-aware losses, and efficient label-generation or student-focused training regimes.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context-Dependent Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a pragmatic pathway to compress large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate representations. Empirical work across vision, speech, language, multimodal and graph domains shows KD can retain much of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in parameters, latency, and memory when combined with complementary compression tools. However, real-world success requires careful choice of teacher signals, data strategies, and optimization protocols to address capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and modality or deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: What is known about Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression strategies form a broad, practically driven toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or specialized teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students. Across modalities and tasks—classification, generation, retrieval, graph learning, self-supervision, and reinforcement learning—research has developed many algorithmic variants (logit and feature matching, attention/relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes), system-level protocols (federated, black-box, data-free), and architecture-aware methods (task-adaptive compression, neural architecture search, pruning and quantization combinations). Empirically, KD often substantially reduces latency and parameter counts while preserving a large fraction of teacher performance, but its success depends on teacher–student alignment, available data and augmentations, and task-specific design; remaining challenges include teacher bias transfer, degradation on low-frequency phenomena, domain shift, and heterogeneous-device constraints. Practical deployments balance distilled signals, data strategies, and architecture choices to achieve required trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, privacy, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied toolkit for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact students. A spectrum of distillation objectives—soft-target/logit matching, intermediate feature and attention alignment, relational and contrastive signals, adversarial or data-free synthesis—together with training protocols (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation) and data strategies (augmentation, mixup, synthetic/zero-shot examples) enables strong empirical gains across vision, language, speech, graph, and generative settings. Practical success depends on matching the distillation objective to student capacity, teacher quality, and available data, and on integrating KD with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Remaining challenges include reliable distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, avoiding propagation of teacher biases and failures on rare phenomena, principled design for heterogeneous architectures and federated settings, and theory-driven choices of what and how to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of the Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: This synthesis summarizes empirical findings, methodological variants, use-cases, limitations, and practical recommendations for knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques in deep learning and NLP. Drawing solely on the provided studies, it highlights common transfer targets and training regimes, domain- and task-specific adaptations, and recurring failure modes, and offers guidance on when and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated family of methods that transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD can materially reduce latency, memory, and energy costs while preserving much of teacher performance, and its variants (logits, intermediate features, attention, relational objectives, online/mutual schemes, and data-free synthesis) extend its applicability across tasks and deployment constraints. However, the benefits of distillation depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and alignment, and the choice of which signals to transfer; practical deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable component integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware practices rather than as a standalone silver bullet.

papers_seen.author: Browning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Context‑Aware Component of Practical Model‑Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated technique for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers across vision, language, recommender, and multimodal tasks. KD routinely delivers substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss when applied with task- and capacity-aware design, but it is not a universal remedy: its success depends on choices of transfer signal, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, distribution shift, and loss of rare behaviors. For reliable production use, KD should be treated as a configurable core element within hybrid compression pipelines that include pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data-aware safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, but Imperfect Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for producing smaller, faster models from large teachers across vision, language, graph, and generative settings. KD supports deployment on constrained hardware, domain adaptation, improved interpretability, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware techniques. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on teacher quality, data and augmentation choices, objective design, and handling of distributional or architectural mismatch. Careful engineering and complementary compression techniques are necessary to realize KD's benefits in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical technique for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models to smaller students. KD methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals, synthetic data) and in protocol (offline, online, self-distillation, many-to-many layer mapping, data-free variants). Empirical results across vision, language, generation, and graph domains demonstrate that distilled students can approach teacher performance when distillation is carefully designed and combined with complementary compression techniques; however, success depends on factors such as teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and explicit mitigation of failure modes including bias transfer and degraded performance on rare phenomena. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline that also uses pretraining, architecture-aware design, and safeguards for privacy and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Beard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of the performance and functionality of larger teacher models. KD is highly versatile—operating at the level of logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational objectives—and is effective across modalities (vision, language, speech, recommender systems, and generative models). However, its practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and distribution, and the design of distillation objectives; consequently KD should be treated as a configurable component that is combined with complementary compression techniques and deployment-aware safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and widely applicable approach to compressing models for deployment in resource-constrained settings. Distillation can transfer many types of knowledge (logits, intermediate features, attention patterns, relational or contrastive signals) and can be adapted to scenarios that lack original training data, require privacy guarantees, or demand task- and hardware-aware compression. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, architecture search, pretraining, or ensemble teaching), KD enables large reductions in model size and latency while largely preserving performance. Nevertheless, distillation can propagate biases and teacher artifacts and needs targeted remedies (feature-focused objectives, multi-teacher strategies, teacher annealing, or exposure to raw data) to avoid failure modes on rare phenomena. The literature demonstrates both the breadth of KD methods and concrete best practices to maximize effectiveness across vision, speech, graph, and NLP tasks.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile family of techniques for compressing large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD variants—ranging from soft-label (logit) matching to feature- and layer-wise imitation, relational and contrastive signals, adversarial or data-free synthesis, and online or multi-teacher protocols—have been shown to recover much of a teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and computational cost. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, availability or synthesis of data, and careful selection of what and how to transfer; open challenges remain in robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare-token/low-frequency behavior, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and enabling private or data-free distillation at scale.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. A diverse set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data-free, federated) together with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search, module replacement) enable substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD’s success is context-dependent: outcomes depend on the choice of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, student capacity, data strategy, and explicit measures to mitigate bias, low-frequency degradation, and distribution shift. Treating KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline and applying task- and data-aware design choices yields the most reliable practical results.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, retrieval, generative modeling, and federated settings. A broad set of techniques—matching soft logits, imitating intermediate features or attention, adversarial and curriculum-based sample selection, ensemble and multi-teacher guidance, and data- or privacy-aware generation—enable students to retain much of teacher performance while reducing parameters, latency, and memory. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often approach teacher performance, but limitations persist (teacher errors, optimization gaps, domain and data mismatch, low-frequency phenomena, and heterogeneity of devices/architectures). Advances such as feature-based distillation, curriculum strategies, adversarial sample use, many-to-many layer alignment, student-friendly teacher design, and teacher-free/self-distillation extend applicability and mitigate failure modes. Key open problems include principled theory for which teacher signals matter across tasks, robust private and data-free distillation, and automated co-design of student architectures and distillation objectives for heterogeneous deployments.

papers_seen.author: Poole
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied compression techniques provide a practical toolkit for shrinking large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their task performance. Over the last decade researchers have developed a range of distillation targets (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention and relational maps, contrastive signals), teacher-student schedules (offline, online, multi-teacher, lifelong), and complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture search, block-structured pruning). Empirical work shows KD often acts both as information transfer and regularization, enabling deployment across vision, language, multimodal, graph, generative, and medical-imaging tasks; however, success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of propagated errors or biases. Best practice is task- and capacity-aware design that combines appropriate distilled signals, alignment of inputs/representations, and complementary compression methods to meet target constraints.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, and Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible suite of methods for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller students. Empirical evidence across vision, language, multimodal, graph, and federated settings shows KD can produce compact models with much of the teacher’s performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD’s practical value increases when combined with complementary compression techniques and when its design is adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints; however, its reliability depends on addressing well-documented failure modes such as teacher–student mismatch, limited or absent data, and propagation of teacher artifacts. This review argues that KD should be treated as a central but context‑aware tool: essential to modern compression pipelines but most effective when paired with targeted algorithmic and engineering practices.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible framework for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. KD encompasses a range of targets and protocols—output-level supervision, intermediate representation matching, adversarial and data-free synthesis, multi-teacher and self-distillation—and is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques. While KD routinely delivers favorable efficiency–accuracy trade-offs in vision, language, recommender, and multimodal systems, realizing those gains in practice requires attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability and privacy, fairness and low-frequency behavior, and method selection for the deployment constraints at hand.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Necessity, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are essential engineering primitives for making large deep models practical in latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained settings. Empirical results across vision, language, and multimodal tasks show that carefully chosen distillation targets, training schedules, and data strategies enable small students to recover much of teacher performance. At the same time, important challenges remain—data heterogeneity, teacher–student mismatch, low-frequency behavior preservation, and principled teacher selection—motivating focused research and deployment practices.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practically essential approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster, or specialized models. When designed around task constraints, student capacity, and available data, KD preserves much of a teacher's capabilities while enabling deployment under compute, memory, latency, and privacy limits. Its greatest value comes from treating distillation as a configurable toolkit—combining soft-targets, representation matching, adversarial or data-free sample synthesis, and multi-teacher or self-distillation—with complementary compression techniques to meet real-world constraints. Success requires careful handling of teacher–student alignment, data scarcity, distribution shift, and bias transfer, but a task-aware, hybrid pipeline makes KD one of the most practical routes to effective model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Configurable Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and broadly effective set of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD reduces latency, memory, and communication costs while often preserving a large fraction of teacher performance; its toolbox includes soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, and protocols ranging from offline to online, multi-teacher, and data-free distillation. However, KD’s success is conditional on task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design). Responsible, robust deployments therefore treat KD as a configurable core within an integrated compression pipeline rather than as a standalone silver bullet.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become core methods for producing compact, efficient models from large teachers across computer vision, speech, graph-based learning, and NLP. Research has diversified beyond the original logits-based teacher-student paradigm into feature- and representation-based distillation, data-free and zero-shot approaches, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, online and adversarial schemes, and task-specific adaptations (e.g., for BERT and non-autoregressive translation). Work also addresses robustness, privacy, few-shot compression, and practical efficiency (reduced compute and communication) for deployment on constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational but Context‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact, deployable models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD succeeds by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations through multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational constraints) and can operate in offline, online, data‑free, and federated regimes. Its empirical strengths span vision, language, speech, multimodal, and distributed training settings. However, KD is not a standalone panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the choice of distilled signals and data strategy, and explicit steps to mitigate transferred biases, low‑frequency failures, and distribution shift. The most reliable compression outcomes treat KD as the practical core of a task‑aware pipeline that integrates representation matching, data and curriculum strategies, and complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Mack
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Dependent Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and broadly applicable family of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD enables meaningful reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often preserving much of teacher performance, but its success is conditional on task- and data-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a turnkey solution.

papers_seen.author: Simpson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task‑Aware Component of Model Compression: Promise, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and versatile approach for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD methods vary in their transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), training paradigms (offline, online, multi‑teacher, meta‑learned teachers, data‑free synthesis), and integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across retrieval, vision, speech, and NLP shows distilled students frequently recover a large fraction of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but reliable deployment requires task‑aware design choices, careful teacher–student alignment, suitable data strategies (including synthesis or privacy‑aware protocols), and explicit safeguards against propagated teacher artifacts and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Simon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, but Insufficient Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, recommendation, and multimodal tasks. KD variants transfer outputs, internal representations, attention patterns, or relational structures and are frequently combined with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies to meet deployment constraints. While KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and supports domain adaptation, privacy-aware training, and robustness improvements, its practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and alignment, and careful objective and architecture design; therefore KD should be treated as a central element of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone cure-all.
